Lilly reports third-quarter 2026 financial results, raises full-year guidance and highlights regulatory progress across the portfolio
October 29, 2026
PDF Version 
Revenue in Q3 2026 increased 39% to $24.4 billion driven primarily by Mounjaro and Zepbound. 
Q3 revenue included approximately $900 million of benefits, primarily from $410 million of Jardiance milestones (no further milestones remain) and favorable adjustments to rebate and discount estimates. 
Q3 2026 EPS increased by 16% to $7.22 on a reported basis and increased by 7% to $7.48 on a non-GAAP basis. Q3 2026 reported and non-GAAP EPS included $4.57 of acquired IPR&D charges compared to $0.71 in Q3 2025. 
Increased the midpoint of our 2026 full-year revenue guidance by $5.5 billion to be in the range of $91.0 to $92.0 billion and raised underlying non-GAAP EPS guidance for the full year by $4.07 at the midpoint, which was more than offset by $4.57 of acquired IPR&D charges from Q3 business development activity, resulting in an updated range of $35.00 to $36.00 . 
Regulatory progress included U.S . FDA approvals of Mounjaro to reduce cardiovascular risk in adults with type 2 diabetes; Onswik, a once-weekly basal insulin for adults with type 2 diabetes; Inluriyo with Verzenio for adults with ER+, HER2-, ESR1-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer; and an expanded indication for Jaypirca in adults with untreated chronic lymphocytic leukemia or small lymphocytic lymphoma. 
Pipeline highlights included positive topline results from a head-to-head Phase 3 trial of retatrutide versus Ozempic 2 mg in adults with type 2 diabetes, Phase 3 results from Ebglyss in moderate-to-severe hand and foot atopic dermatitis and Phase 2 results from EloraTZP in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes, with Phase 3 trials to start in Q4 2026. 
Business development activity in Q3 2026 included the completed acquisition of AtaiBeckley to advance therapies for treatment-resistant depression and other mental health conditions. Subsequent to quarter end, we completed the acquisition of Merida Biosciences, to advance treatments for serious autoimmune and allergic diseases. 
INDIANAPOLIS , Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Eli Lilly and Company (NYSE: LLY) today announced its financial results for the third quarter of 2026 and provided updated 2026 financial guidance.
" Lilly had another strong quarter, exceeding our prior expectations and allowing us to raise our full-year outlook," said David A. Ricks , Lilly chair and CEO. "Revenue growth was driven by broad global consumer demand for Mounjaro and Zepbound, the global launches of Foundayo, expanded U.S . coverage for obesity care and a doubling in our newest products in oncology, immunology and neuroscience. To drive durable long-term growth, we continue to invest in our drug-making and technology capabilities, with multiple business development deals and partnerships signed and closed, and with new manufacturing expansions in Texas and Virginia . Lilly is executing well across the value chain, and our potential for impact on human health continues to expand."

Third-Quarter Reported Results
In Q3 2026, worldwide revenue was $24.4 billion , an increase of 39% compared with Q3 2025, driven by a 53% increase in volume, partially offset by a 15% decrease in realized prices. Key Products 1 revenue grew to $17.1 billion in Q3 2026, led by Mounjaro and Zepbound. Key Products revenue in the Immunology, Oncology, and Neuroscience therapeutic areas grew 100% in Q3 2026 compared to Q3 2025.
Revenue in the U.S . increased 34% to $15.1 billion , driven by a 41% increase in volume, partially offset by a 7% decrease in realized prices. The increase in U.S . volume was driven by Zepbound and Mounjaro. The decline in realized prices was primarily driven by Zepbound, partially offset by adjustments to estimates for rebates and discounts.
Revenue outside the U.S . increased 47% to $9.3 billion , driven by a 76% increase in volume, partially offset by a 29% decrease in realized prices. The volume increase outside the U.S . was driven by Mounjaro. Jardiance revenue outside the U.S . included sales-based milestones of $410 million in Q3 2026 and $200 million in Q3 2025, associated with the company's collaboration with Boehringer Ingelheim . Additionally, Q3 2025 revenue included $180 million associated with the divestiture of the rights to Cialis in select markets outside of the U.S . Lower realized prices outside the U.S . were driven primarily by the inclusion of Mounjaro on the National Reimbursement Drug List (NRDL) in China .
Gross margin increased 40% to $20.5 billion in Q3 2026. Gross margin as a percent of revenue was 83.9%, an increase of 1.0 percentage points versus the same quarter last year. The increase was primarily driven by favorable product mix and improved cost of production, partially offset by lower realized prices.
In Q3 2026, research and development expenses increased 23% to $4.2 billion , or 17% of revenue, driven by continued investments in the company's early and late-stage portfolio.
Marketing, selling, and administrative expenses increased 14% to $3.1 billion in Q3 2026, primarily driven by promotional efforts supporting ongoing and planned launches.
In Q3 2026, the company recognized acquired in-process research and development (IPR&D) charges of $4.2 billion compared with $656 million in Q3 2025. The Q3 2026 charges primarily related to the acquisitions of AtaiBeckley Inc. and Curevo Inc. 
The effective tax rate was 23.3% in Q3 2026 compared with 22.8% in Q3 2025, primarily driven by the unfavorable tax impact of nondeductible acquired IPR&D charges, with a larger impact occurring in 2026. The Q3 2025 effective tax rate was also unfavorably impacted by U.S . tax law changes.
In Q3 2026, net income and earnings per share (EPS) were $6 .5 billion and $7.22 , respectively, compared with net income of $5 .6 billion and EPS of $6.21 in Q3 2025. EPS in Q3 2026 and Q3 2025 included acquired IPR&D charges of $4.57 and $0.71 , respectively.
1 The Company currently defines Key Products as Ebglyss, Foundayo, Inluriyo, Jaypirca, Kisunla, Mounjaro, Omvoh, and Zepbound. 
Third-Quarter Non-GAAP Measures
On a non-GAAP basis, Q3 2026 gross margin increased 40% to $20.6 billion . Gross margin as a percent of revenue was 84.4%, an increase of 0.8 percentage points versus the same quarter last year. The increase was primarily driven by favorable product mix and improved cost of production, partially offset by lower realized prices.
The non-GAAP effective tax rate was 24.0% in Q3 2026 compared with 17.7% in Q3 2025, primarily driven by the unfavorable tax impact of nondeductible acquired IPR&D charges, with a larger impact occurring in 2026.
On a non-GAAP basis, Q3 2026 net income and EPS were $6.7 billion and $7.48 , respectively, compared with net income of $6 .3 billion and EPS of $7.02 in Q3 2025. Non-GAAP EPS in Q3 2026 and Q3 2025 included acquired IPR&D charges of $4.57 and $0.71 , respectively.

Zepbound

Lilly shared numerous updates recently on key regulatory, clinical, business development, and other events, including:
Regulatory 
Lilly 's Jaypirca (pirtobrutinib), the first-and-only approved non-covalent BTK 
inhibitor, receives expanded indication from U.S . FDA for certain patients with 
previously untreated CLL/SLL ( announcement ) 
FDA approves Lilly 's Olumiant (baricitinib) for pediatric patients 12 years of age and 
older with severe alopecia areata ( announcement ) 
U.S. Food and Drug Administration ( FDA ) approves Lilly 's Onswik™ (insulin
efsitora alfa-gobe), a once-weekly basal insulin injection treatment for adults living 
with type 2 diabetes ( announcement ) 
U.S . FDA approves Inluriyo (imlunestrant) in combination with Verzenio 
(abemaciclib) for adults with ER+, HER2-, ESR1-mutated advanced or metastatic 
breast cancer ( announcement ) 
FDA approves Lilly 's Mounjaro (tirzepatide) to reduce cardiovascular risk in adults 
with type 2 diabetes ( announcement ) 
Clinical 
Lilly 's retatrutide delivered greater A1C reduction and more than double the weight 
loss of Ozempic's highest approved dose in head-to-head trial ( announcement ) 
New data on Lilly 's investigational treatment olomorasib at ESMO 2026 show 
durable first-line activity in KRAS G12C-mutant non-small cell lung cancer 
( announcement ) 
Lilly presents first clinical data in platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer for its 
investigational, next-generation, FRα-targeting ADC at ESMO 2026 
( announcement ) 
Lilly 's Omvoh (mirikizumab-mrkz) meets primary endpoint of clinical remission and 
is the first IL-23p19 inhibitor to report one-year Phase 3 results in pediatric 
ulcerative colitis ( announcement ) 
New composite outcomes data show patients treated with Lilly 's Omvoh 
(mirikizumab-mrkz) achieved comprehensive corticosteroid-free disease control in 
ulcerative colitis and corticosteroid-free deep remission in Crohn's disease at one 
year ( announcement ) 
New Phase 3b data on Lilly 's Taltz (ixekizumab) and Zepbound (tirzepatide) 
advance understanding of the interconnected immune and metabolic biology in 
adults with psoriasis and obesity ( announcement ) 
Lilly 's oral GLP-1, Foundayo (orforglipron), demonstrated cardiovascular safety 
alongside sustained A1C reduction and weight loss in its largest and longest type 2 
diabetes study ( announcement ) 
Lilly 's EloraTZP (combination of eloralintide and tirzepatide) delivered greater 
weight loss and A1C reduction vs. tirzepatide 15 mg in adults with obesity and type 
2 diabetes ( announcement ) 
New Phase 3b data show Lilly 's EBGLYSS (lebrikizumab-lbkz) delivered significant 
and rapid improvements in skin clearance, itch, pain, and patient satisfaction in 
people with moderate-to-severe hand and foot atopic dermatitis ( announcement ) 
Lilly 's triple agonist, retatrutide, delivered substantial weight loss and A1C 
reduction, underscoring its potential promise for people with obesity and type 2 
diabetes ( announcement ) 
New Phase 3b data on Lilly 's Taltz (ixekizumab) and Zepbound (tirzepatide) used 
together showed improved and durable efficacy at one year in adults with psoriatic 
disease and obesity ( announcement ) 
Other 
Patrik Jonsson to retire after 36 years; Ilya Yuffa named president, Lilly Global 
Markets ( announcement ) 
Lilly breaks ground in Richmond to expand American manufacturing of next-
generation cancer medicines, advancing its build-out of 10 new U.S . sites since 
2020 ( announcement ) 
Lilly launches the Lilly Change the Course Commitment, aiming to address 
treatment gaps in diabetes and obesity in LMICs ( ann ouncement ) 
Lilly breaks ground in Houston , one of ten U.S . manufacturing sites announced 
since 2020 ( announce ment ) 
Lilly completes acquisition of AtaiBeckley to advance therapies for treatment-
resistant depression and other mental health conditions ( announcement ) 
Lilly to acquire Merida Biosciences to advance treatments for serious autoimmune 
and allergic diseases ( announcement ) 
Zepbound linked to lower healthcare costs in adults over age 55 with obesity 
according to a real-world study ( announcement ) 
Lilly calls on online platforms, payment companies and regulators to shut down the 
illegal retatrutide black market ( announcement ) 
For information on important public announcements, visit the news section of Lilly 's website.

As previously announced, investors and the general public can access a live webcast of the Q3 2026 financial results conference call through a link on Lilly 's website at investor.lilly.com/webcasts-and-presentations . The conference call will begin at 10 a.m. Eastern time today and will be available for replay via the website.
Non-GAAP Financial Measures
Certain financial information is presented on both a reported and a non-GAAP basis. Some numbers in this press release may not add due to rounding. Reported results were prepared in accordance with U.S . generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) and include all revenue and expenses recognized during the periods. Historical non-GAAP measures reflect adjustments for the items described in the reconciliation tables later in the release. Related materials provide certain GAAP and non-GAAP figures excluding the impact of foreign exchange rates. Lilly recalculates current period figures on a constant currency basis by keeping constant the exchange rates from the base period. The company's 2026 financial guidance (other than revenue) is provided on a non-GAAP basis, as described in "2026 Financial Guidance" above. Non-GAAP measures are presented to provide additional insights into the underlying trends in the company's business.
About Lilly 
Lilly is a medicine company turning science into healing to make life better for people around the world. We've been pioneering life-changing discoveries for 150 years, and today our medicines help tens of millions of people across the globe. Harnessing the power of biotechnology, chemistry and genetic medicine, our scientists are urgently advancing new discoveries to solve some of the world's most significant health challenges: redefining diabetes care; treating obesity and curtailing its most devastating long-term effects; advancing the fight against Alzheimer's disease; providing solutions to some of the most debilitating immune system disorders; and transforming the most difficult-to-treat cancers into manageable diseases. With each step toward a healthier world, we're motivated by one thing: making life better for millions more people. That includes delivering innovative clinical trials that reflect the diversity of our world and working to ensure our medicines are accessible and affordable. To learn more, visit Lilly.com and Lilly.com/news . F-LLY

GE HealthCare reports third quarter 2026 financial results
October 28, 2026
PDF Version 
Delivers top- and bottom-line growth ahead of Company expectations and raises full-year 2026 guidance
Revenue growth of 7.2%, and Organic revenue growth* of 6.2%
Organic orders growth of 4.0%, book-to-bill of 1.03 times and backlog of $23.7 billion 
Net income margin of 11.1% and Adjusted earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) margin* of 16.6%; diluted EPS of $1.36 grew 39.1% and Adjusted EPS* of $1.34 grew 25.1%
Cash flow from operating activities of $907 million and Free cash flow* of $793 million 
CHICAGO --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 28, 2026--
GE HealthCare (Nasdaq: GEHC) today reported financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026 .
GE HealthCare President and CEO Peter Arduini said, “We delivered strong top-line growth and margin expansion across all segments, and robust EPS growth in the third quarter. This reflects our teams’ commercial execution, disciplined operational focus enabled by Heartbeat, and continued customer adoption of our innovations. With our improved performance year-to-date and momentum in the business, we are raising guidance for the year.”
Third quarter 2026 total company financial performance (1) 
Revenues of $5.5 billion , up 7.2%, including Organic revenue growth* of 6.2%, with growth across all segments.
Total orders up 4.0% organically, book-to-bill of 1.03 times and backlog of $23.7 billion , driven by healthy demand.
Net income attributable to GE HealthCare of $615 million versus $446 million , and Adjusted EBIT* of $913 million versus $761 million .
Net income margin of 11.1% versus 8.7%, up 250 basis points (bps). Adjusted EBIT margin* of 16.6% versus 14.8%, up 180 bps, with both measures driven by volume, price and cost productivity, and favorable year-over-year net tariff impact, partially offset by inflation.
Diluted EPS of $1.36 versus $0.98 , up $0.38 ; Adjusted EPS* of $1.34 versus $1.07 , up $0.27 .

Non-GAAP financial measures 
The non-GAAP financial measures presented in this press release are supplemental measures of GE HealthCare’s performance and its liquidity that the Company believes will help investors understand its financial condition, cash flows, and operating results, and assess its future prospects. When read in conjunction with the Company’s U.S . GAAP results, these non-GAAP financial measures provide a baseline for analyzing trends in GE HealthCare’s underlying businesses and can be used by management as one basis for making financial, operational, and planning decisions. Descriptions of the reported non-GAAP measures are included below.
The Company reports Organic revenue and Organic revenue growth rate to provide management and investors with additional understanding and visibility into the underlying revenue trends of the Company’s established, ongoing operations, as well as provide insights into overall demand for its products and services. To calculate these measures, the Company excludes the effect of acquisitions, dispositions, and foreign currency rate fluctuations.
The Company reports EBIT, Adjusted EBIT, Adjusted EBIT margin, Adjusted net income, and Adjusted earnings per share to provide management and investors with an additional understanding of its business by highlighting the results from ongoing operations and the underlying profitability factors, on a normalized basis. To calculate these measures the Company excludes, and reflects in the detailed reconciliations below, the following adjustments as applicable: Interest and other financial charges – net, Net (income) loss attributable to noncontrolling interests, Non-operating benefit (income) costs, Benefit (provision) for income taxes and certain tax related adjustments, and certain non-recurring and/or non-cash items. GE HealthCare may from time to time consider excluding other non-recurring items to enhance comparability between periods. Adjusted EBIT margin is calculated by taking Adjusted EBIT divided by Total revenues for the same period.
The Company reports Adjusted tax expense and Adjusted ETR to provide management and investors with a better understanding of the normalized tax rate applicable to the business and provide more consistent comparability across periods. Adjusted tax expense excludes the income tax related to the pre-tax income adjustments included as part of Adjusted net income and certain income tax adjustments, such as adjustments to deferred tax assets or liabilities. The Company may from time to time consider excluding other non-recurring tax items to enhance comparability between periods. Adjusted ETR is Adjusted tax expense divided by income before income taxes less the pre-tax income adjustments referenced above.
The Company reports Free cash flow and Free cash flow conversion to provide management and investors with an important measure of the ability to generate cash on a normalized basis and provide insight into the Company’s flexibility to allocate capital. Free cash flow is Cash from (used for) operating activities – continuing operations including cash flows related to the additions and dispositions of property, plant, and equipment (“PP&E”) and additions of internal-use software. Free cash flow does not represent residual cash flows available for discretionary expenditures, due to the fact that the measure does not deduct the capital required for debt repayments. Free cash flow conversion is calculated by taking Free cash flow divided by Adjusted net income.
Management recognizes that these non-GAAP financial measures have limitations, including that they may be calculated differently by other companies or may be used under different circumstances or for different purposes. In order to compensate for the discussed limitations, management does not consider these measures in isolation from or as alternatives to the comparable financial measures determined in accordance with U.S . GAAP. The detailed reconciliations of each non-GAAP financial measure to the most directly comparable U.S . GAAP financial measure are provided below, and no single financial measure should be relied on to evaluate our business.

Non-GAAP financial measures in outlook 
GE HealthCare calculates forward-looking non-GAAP financial measures, including Organic revenue growth, Adjusted EBIT margin, Adjusted ETR, Adjusted EPS, and Free cash flow based on internal forecasts that omit certain amounts that would be included in U.S . Key performance indicators 
Management uses the following metrics to provide a leading indicator of current business demand from customers for products and services.

title: Six Companies Launch Joint R&D to Build a Quantum-Computing-Based Materials Development Platform
query: https://www.holdings.toppan.com/en/news/
content_text:
Six Companies Launch Joint R&D to Build a Quantum-Computing-Based Materials Development Platform
Project selected by NEDO for innovative materials development platforms using quantum technology; demonstrates practical use cases that integrate quantum computing and AI technologies
Tweet 
Tokyo – October 28, 2026 –TOPPAN Holdings Inc. (TOPPAN Holdings; TYO: 7911), AISIN CORPORATION (AISIN; TYO: 7259), Asahi Kasei Corporation (Asahi Kasei; TYO: 3407), SoftBank Corp. (SoftBank; TYO: 9434), AGC Inc. (AGC; TYO: 5201), and DIC Corporation (DIC; TYO: 4631) jointly announced today that their joint proposal, “Research and Development of Innovative Materials Development Platforms Using Quantum Technology” (hereinafter the “Project”), has been selected by the New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization (NEDO). 1 The Project was chosen under NEDO’s solicitation for the “Research and Development Project of the Enhanced Infrastructures for Post-5G Information and Communication Systems ”.
Following this selection, the six companies entered into a joint agreement to conduct research and development on constructing a new materials development platform utilizing quantum computers from fiscal 2026 (the year ending March 31, 2027) through fiscal 2028. The Project aims to establish a next-generation materials development platform by integrating quantum-computing-based calculations with AI technologies such as machine learning, thereby bridging the gap between demonstration and real-world application.
Background
For Japanese chemical and materials manufacturers to maintain global competitiveness, an urgent priority is to establish technologies that dramatically improve the discovery of new materials as well as development efficiency. In recent years, progress has been made in data-driven approaches—where AI predicts and explores new materials based on historical materials data—as well as computational science simulations based on physical laws. However, while data-driven methods face a challenge in securing sufficient, high-quality, and high-precision training data, computational science faces the issue of surging computational costs for higher accuracy and larger scale calculations. 
There is strong optimism for quantum computers operating on the principles of quantum mechanics to address such challenges. Quantum computers have the potential to simulate the properties of molecules and electrons governed by quantum mechanics more efficiently than conventional computers. However, since there are currently limitations in qubit 2 count and error rates, large-scale calculations using quantum computers alone are still not a reality.
To overcome these hurdles, the Project will establish a methodology that combines quantum-computing-based calculations with AI, mitigating constraints on calculation precision and scale. Rather than targeting a single specific material, the materials development technologies will be applied cross-sectionally across a broad range of industrially vital materials systems, with each of the six companies handling verification in their respective domains of strength. In addition, through collaboration with specialized quantum computing institutions, the companies will advance applicability verifications across diverse materials while working together to create practical value for industrial application.
Overview of the Project
1. Verification of Quantum Computing Application Areas 
Verify the applicability of quantum computing for numerous major materials with high industrial demand, including materials required for next-generation batteries, optical functional materials for new displays and sensors, and superconducting materials for next-generation devices. 
2. Development of Quantum Computing Utilization Technologies 
Develop technologies that integrate quantum-computing-based calculations with AI to expand the scope of computational methods and verify solutions to scale and cost limitations inherent in conventional computing methods. 
3. Simulation Demonstration and Experiment Feedback 
Synthesize materials and evaluate their performance based on simulation results (including those using quantum computing) and compare experiment results against simulation data to improve predictive accuracy and verify the benefits of practical application of quantum computing. 
Roles of Participating Companies
TOPPAN Holdings 
Execute hybrid methods combining quantum and classical algorithms on quantum computers for additive materials to verify quantum computing application; develop combined quantum computing and AI methods; provide experiment feedback. 
AISIN 
Verify quantum computing application for superconducting materials; compare results with conventional material development methods; forecast practical implementation timelines in material development environments.
Asahi Kasei 
Verify platforms utilizing quantum computing for materials development through applicability studies of quantum computing to organic compounds (such as electrolytes), polymer materials, and inorganic materials (such as electrodes), combined with feedback from experimental results.
SoftBank Corp. 
Utilize a computing platform connecting quantum computers with supercomputers to generate high-level data useful for material development, along with developing data utilization technologies using AI; carry out demonstrations to optimize material development across diverse domains, including energy-related materials such as next-generation batteries. 
AGC 
Develop and evaluate material development methods combining quantum computing with existing computational science and AI technologies for inorganic materials (such as optical glass) and organic materials (such as electronic materials); derive insights and establish design guidelines to enhance materials exploration and design. 
DIC 
Integrate quantum computing, simulation, and data science technologies to predict key material properties prior to synthesis for colorants and semiconductor materials, while establishing and validating novel research methodologies that accelerate the efficient design and development of high-performance materials.
Future Steps
By combining data on quantum computing and AI with the experimental data obtained through the Project, the six companies will work toward constructing a continuously evolving materials development platform, contributing to the creation of cross-industry innovation.
1 For details on the call for proposals and selection results, please visit: https://www.nedo.go.jp/koubo/CD3_100424.html (in Japanese)
2 A qubit is the fundamental unit of quantum information in quantum computing.

Oct. 28, 2026
Veolia Jenets K.K.
Sumitomo Chemical Co., Ltd.
Veolia Jenets K.K. (“Veolia”) and Sumitomo Chemical Co., Ltd. (“Sumitomo Chemical”) have been selected to participate in the Ministry of the Environment of Japan’s FY2026 Model Project for Plastic Resource Circulation (the “Model Project”). By combining Mechanical Recycling (“MR”) and chemical recycling (“CR”), the two companies aim to advance resource utilization rates and conversion rates into chemicals in the recycling of plastic containers and packaging.
Up until now, plastic containers and packaging separately collected under Japan’s Containers and Packaging Recycling Act (“collected plastic containers and packaging”) have been handled by recycling operators and then recycled using either MR or CR as the sole recycling method. Beginning in FY2027, the System will enable MR operators and CR operators to form joint groups and combine different recycling methods to further advance in quality and yield of the recycling of collected plastic packaging. The Model Project is intended to promote the use of the System.
Some collected plastic containers and packaging are difficult to make efficient use of due to differences in material composition, contamination, or the use of composite materials. As a result, conventional MR has achieved a recycling rate of only approximately 50% for collected plastic containers and packaging.* Through participation in the Model Project, waste plastics derived from residues generated during the MR process will be recycled through CR. This combined approach is expected to increase the resource utilization rate of collected plastic containers and packaging to approximately 80%. In addition, CR will enable waste plastics from residues generated in the MR process, which have previously been used mainly for energy recovery, to be recycled into chemicals of equivalent quality to fossil-derived virgin products, expanding their use to include chemical feedstocks.
Under the Model Project, drawing on its expertise in waste management, sorting, and resource recovery, Veolia will promote the efficient use of materials suitable for MR while developing a sorting and supply scheme to channel plastics difficult to process through MR to CR. Through these efforts, Veolia aims to improve the resource utilization rate and add greater value to recycled resources. Sumitomo Chemical will seek to apply its CR technology to efficiently convert pyrolysis oil derived from plastics sorted and supplied by Veolia for CR into basic chemicals, such as ethylene and propylene, using a proprietary catalyst currently under development. 
Veolia and Sumitomo Chemical will leverage the results of the studies and verification conducted under the Model Project and strengthen their collaboration with a wide range of stakeholders—including municipalities, recycling operators, product manufacturers, and customers. Through these efforts, the two companies will seek to achieve the practical implementation of a resource-circulation scheme and CR technology and contribute to the realization of a circular society.
About Veolia Jenets
Veolia Jenets K.K. is a group company of Veolia, a global leader in environmental services. Established in 1997, it operates an integrated portfolio of water, waste, and energy businesses in Japan. Leveraging expertise developed both globally and domestically, it provides locally rooted services throughout Japan.
In the waste sector, Veolia collects, sorts, and recycles plastics, including plastic containers and packaging, thereby supporting the transition to a circular economy.
About Sumitomo Chemical
Sumitomo Chemical is a diversified chemical company that supports a broad range of industries, and the everyday lives of people, through its Agro & Life Solutions, ICT & Mobility Solutions, and Advanced Medical Solutions businesses, Essential & Green Materials. The Company regards resource circulation and the reduction of GHG emissions as key priorities, and promotes the development and practical implementation of technologies, products, and businesses, including chemical recycling.
 
*Source: Research Report: Estimated Effective Utilization Rates by Plastic Type (FY2024), The Japan Containers and Packaging Recycling Association.

TOPPAN Holdings Inc. (TOPPAN Holdings; TYO: 7911), AISIN CORPORATION (AISIN; TYO: 7259), Asahi Kasei Corporation (Asahi Kasei; TYO: 3407), SoftBank Corp. (SoftBank; TYO: 9434), AGC Inc. (AGC; TYO: 5201), and DIC Corporation (DIC; TYO: 4631) jointly announced today that their joint proposal, “Research and Development of Innovative Materials Development Platforms Using Quantum Technology” (hereinafter the “Project”), has been selected by the New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization (NEDO). 1 The Project was chosen under NEDO’s solicitation for the “Research and Development Project of the Enhanced Infrastructures for Post-5G Information and Communication Systems ”.
Following this selection, the six companies entered into a joint agreement to conduct research and development on constructing a new materials development platform utilizing quantum computers from fiscal 2026 (the year ending March 31, 2027) through fiscal 2028. The Project aims to establish a next-generation materials development platform by integrating quantum-computing-based calculations with AI technologies such as machine learning, thereby bridging the gap between demonstration and real-world application.
Background 
For Japanese chemical and materials manufacturers to maintain global competitiveness, an urgent priority is to establish technologies that dramatically improve the discovery of new materials as well as development efficiency. In recent years, progress has been made in data-driven approaches—where AI predicts and explores new materials based on historical materials data—as well as computational science simulations based on physical laws. However, while data-driven methods face a challenge in securing sufficient, high-quality, and high-precision training data, computational science faces the issue of surging computational costs for higher accuracy and larger scale calculations.
There is strong optimism for quantum computers operating on the principles of quantum mechanics to address such challenges. Quantum computers have the potential to simulate the properties of molecules and electrons governed by quantum mechanics more efficiently than conventional computers. However, since there are currently limitations in qubit 2 count and error rates, large-scale calculations using quantum computers alone are still not a reality.
To overcome these hurdles, the Project will establish a methodology that combines quantum-computing-based calculations with AI, mitigating constraints on calculation precision and scale. Rather than targeting a single specific material, the materials development technologies will be applied cross-sectionally across a broad range of industrially vital materials systems, with each of the six companies handling verification in their respective domains of strength. In addition, through collaboration with specialized quantum computing institutions, the companies will advance applicability verifications across diverse materials while working together to create practical value for industrial application.
Overview of the Project 
1. Verification of Quantum Computing Application Areas 
Verify the applicability of quantum computing for numerous major materials with high industrial demand, including materials required for next-generation batteries, optical functional materials for new displays and sensors, and superconducting materials for next-generation devices.
2. Development of Quantum Computing Utilization Technologies 
Develop technologies that integrate quantum-computing-based calculations with AI to expand the scope of computational methods and verify solutions to scale and cost limitations inherent in conventional computing methods.
3. Simulation Demonstration and Experiment Feedback 
Synthesize materials and evaluate their performance based on simulation results (including those using quantum computing) and compare experiment results against simulation data to improve predictive accuracy and verify the benefits of practical application of quantum computing.
Roles of Participating Companies
TOPPAN Holdings 
Execute hybrid methods combining quantum and classical algorithms on quantum computers for additive materials to verify quantum computing application; develop combined quantum computing and AI methods; provide experiment feedback.
AISIN 
Verify quantum computing application for superconducting materials; compare results with conventional material development methods; forecast practical implementation timelines in material development environments.
Asahi Kasei 
Verify platforms utilizing quantum computing for materials development through applicability studies of quantum computing to organic compounds (such as electrolytes), polymer materials, and inorganic materials (such as electrodes), combined with feedback from experimental results.
SoftBank Corp. 
Utilize a computing platform connecting quantum computers with supercomputers to generate high-level data useful for material development, along with developing data utilization technologies using AI; carry out demonstrations to optimize material development across diverse domains, including energy-related materials such as next-generation batteries.
AGC 
Develop and evaluate material development methods combining quantum computing with existing computational science and AI technologies for inorganic materials (such as optical glass) and organic materials (such as electronic materials); derive insights and establish design guidelines to enhance materials exploration and design.
DIC 
Integrate quantum computing, simulation, and data science technologies to predict key material properties prior to synthesis for colorants and semiconductor materials, while establishing and validating novel research methodologies that accelerate the efficient design and development of high-performance materials.
Future Steps 
By combining data on quantum computing and AI with the experimental data obtained through the Project, the six companies will work toward constructing a continuously evolving materials development platform, contributing to the creation of cross-industry innovation.
1 For details on the call for proposals and selection results, please visit: https://www.nedo.go.jp/koubo/CD3_100424.html (in Japanese)
2 A qubit is the fundamental unit of quantum information in quantum computing.

title: Patrik Jonsson to retire after 36 years; Ilya Yuffa named president, Lilly Global Markets
source: Eli Lilly and Company - Official RSS

Patrik Jonsson to retire after 36 years; Ilya Yuffa named president, Lilly Global Markets
October 27, 2026
PDF Version 
Yuffa will take on an expanded role as the company scales for its next phase of growth 
Key highlights: 
Patrik Jonsson , executive vice president and president, Lilly International , has decided to retire at the end of 2026 after a 36-year career at Lilly .
On Jan. 1, 2027 , Ilya Yuffa will take on an expanded role as executive vice president and president, Lilly Global Markets, overseeing customer strategy and execution worldwide.
Laura Steele will be promoted to president, Lilly USA , and Elias Khalil will be promoted to group vice president and president, Lilly Europe and Canada .
INDIANAPOLIS , Oct. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Eli Lilly and Company (NYSE: LLY) today announced that Patrik Jonsson , executive vice president and president, Lilly International , has decided to retire at the end of 2026 after a 36-year career at Lilly .
Jonsson joined the company in 1990 as a sales representative in Sweden . He went on to lead Lilly in Sweden , Scandinavia, Italy and Japan, then served as president of Lilly Bio-Medicines and Lilly Immunology, as well as president of Lilly USA and Lilly 's cardiometabolic health business, before leading Lilly International .
"For more than three decades, Patrik has dedicated his career to improving lives by bringing our medicines to people around the world," said David A. Ricks , Lilly chair and CEO. "He has held multiple executive roles in the company spanning drug development and customer operations, including head of immunology, cardiometabolic health and Lilly USA . Today he applies his deep expertise in global launches across Lilly International . Patrik is a patient-focused, engaging team leader who has mentored countless colleagues. On behalf of our Board, leadership team and thousands of employees he has worked alongside, I thank Patrik for his service to our company."
Effective Jan. 1, 2027 , Lilly 's U.S . and international businesses will come together as Lilly Global Markets, led by Ilya Yuffa , who will become executive vice president and president, Lilly Global Markets.
Bringing these organizations together will accelerate decision-making, increase scalability and provide a unified capability to improve human health through expanded access to medicines around the world.
Yuffa joined Lilly in 1996 as a financial analyst and has held leadership roles in finance, business development, sales and general management, including president and general manager of Lilly 's Italy Hub, which covered more than 25 countries, president of Lilly Bio-Medicines, president of Lilly International and currently executive vice president and president, Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities.
Ricks continued, "To build on our momentum, now is the right time to consolidate our geographies for greater impact. Ilya has run both our international and U.S . businesses, and his range of experience and commitment to excellence make him uniquely qualified to lead our customer-facing operations worldwide. He is joined by a proven team with the expertise and focus to help us reach even more people with our medicines."
The following executives will lead the company's six geographic hubs and report to Yuffa:
Laura Steele , currently group vice president, U.S. Cardiometabolic Health , will be promoted to president, Lilly USA . In 23 years at Lilly , Steele has held leadership roles in marketing, value and access, and commercial operations inside and outside the U.S ., including Lilly 's U.S . neuroscience business.
Elias Khalil , currently president and general manager of Lilly 's Italy Hub, will be promoted to group vice president and president, Lilly Europe and Canada . In 18 years at Lilly , Khalil has held leadership roles across the Gulf region, Saudi Arabia and the U.S . neuroscience business.
Nabil Daoud will continue in his role as group vice president and president, Lilly InterContinental.
Karla Alcazar , Huzur Devletsah and Winselow Tucker will continue in their roles as president and general manager of Lilly Japan , Lilly China and Lilly India , respectively.
About Lilly 
Lilly is a medicine company turning science into healing to make life better for people around the world. We've been pioneering life-changing discoveries for 150 years, and today our medicines help tens of millions of people across the globe. Harnessing the power of biotechnology, chemistry and genetic medicine, our scientists are urgently advancing new discoveries to solve some of the world's most significant health challenges: redefining diabetes care; treating obesity and curtailing its most devastating long-term effects; advancing the fight against Alzheimer's disease; providing solutions to some of the most debilitating immune system disorders; and transforming the most difficult-to-treat cancers into manageable diseases. With each step toward a healthier world, we're motivated by one thing: making life better for millions more people. That includes delivering innovative clinical trials that reflect the diversity of our world and working to ensure our medicines are accessible and affordable. To learn more, visit Lilly.com and Lilly.com/news , or follow us on Facebook , Instagram , and LinkedIn . C-LLY
Trademarks and Trade Names 
All trademarks or trade names referred to in this press release are the property of the company, or, to the extent trademarks or trade names belonging to other companies are referenced in this press release, the property of their respective owners. Solely for convenience, the trademarks and trade names in this press release are referred to without the ® and ™ symbols, but such references should not be construed as any indicator that the company or, to the extent applicable, their respective owners will not assert, to the fullest extent under applicable law, the company's or their rights thereto. We do not intend the use or display of other companies' trademarks and trade names to imply a relationship with, or endorsement or sponsorship of us by, any other companies.
Cautionary Statement Regarding Forward-Looking Statements 
This press release contains forward-looking statements (as that term is defined in the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995) about Lilly's leadership changes and the creation of Lilly global initiatives and reflects Lilly's current beliefs and expectations. However, there can be no assurance that these actions will achieve Lilly's objectives or that Lilly will execute its strategy as planned. Charles River Leverages Virtual Control Groups in GLP Studies
PDF Version 
Collaboration highlights ongoing commitment to industry modernization and the highest animal welfare standards 
WILMINGTON, Mass. --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 27, 2026--
Charles River Laboratories International, Inc. (NYSE: CRL) today announced that its Virtual Control Group (VCG) database and methodology, aimed at reducing animal use, will be used in an upcoming Good Laboratory Practice (GLP)-compliant study for Ipsen. This collaboration highlights Charles River’s and Ipsen’s dedication and commitment to championing the 3Rs (Replacement, Reduction, and Refinement of animal use in research) while upholding the highest scientific standards. Charles River’s VCG program operates under the Alternative Methods Advancement Project™ (AMAP™), an initiative aimed at minimizing animal use in research whenever scientifically appropriate.
“This partnership exemplifies Charles River’s scientific leadership and commitment to modernizing our company and the industry,” said Dr. Namandjé N. Bumpus , Chief Scientific and Innovation Officer, Charles River. “By advancing VCGs, we are driving innovation for safety studies and reducing animal use where scientifically appropriate.”
By combining toxicology and regulatory expertise, historical control data, advanced statistical methods, and AI-powered analytics, VCGs can digitally replace a portion of concurrent control animals in safety studies. This approach lessens reliance on animal use while enhancing data clarity, offering a modern, ethical, and scientifically robust solution for developers seeking efficient decision-making. Charles River will supply VCG data to Ipsen to facilitate prospective analysis of general toxicology endpoints.
Advancing Virtual Control Groups 
Virtual Control Groups may be able to impact study timelines, enhance data quality, and meet evolving regulatory expectations for the 3Rs .
Up to 12% reduction in animal use where scientifically appropriate, without compromising regulatory-grade rigor
Greater statistical power, particularly for detecting rare spontaneous findings that may otherwise obscure study outcomes
More consistent interpretation, leveraging large, curated historical datasets to contextualize unexpected results
As Charles River continues to advance innovative approaches through AMAP, collaborations like this demonstrate how science, technology, and expertise can work together to reduce animal use while maintaining the rigorous standards required to bring new therapies to patients.
About the Alternative Methods Advancement Project (AMAP)
The Alternative Methods Advancement Project (AMAP) is a Charles River-led initiative dedicated to developing New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) and exploring innovative scientific and technological solutions aimed at reducing reliance on traditional animal testing. As we enter the next frontier of drug development, AMAP enables strategic, purpose-driven investment to shape a future in which more patients can access the treatments and medicines they need safely, swiftly, and successfully. AMAP is supported by our global, cross-functional Scientific Advisory Board led by Dr. Namandjé N. Bumpus .
About Charles River
Charles River provides essential products and services to help pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, government agencies and leading academic institutions around the globe accelerate their research and drug development efforts. Our dedicated employees are focused on providing clients with exactly what they need to improve and expedite the discovery, early-stage development and safe manufacture of new therapies for the patients who need them. To learn more about our unique portfolio and breadth of services, visit www.criver.com .

Applied Materials to Increase its Strategic Investment in BE Semiconductor Industries
Duiven, the Netherlands, October 27, 2026 - BE Semiconductor Industries N.V. (the “Company” or “Besi”) (Euronext Amsterdam: BESI; OTC markets: BESIY), a leading manufacturer of assembly equipment for the semiconductor industry, acknowledged today the press release from Applied Materials, Inc. (“Applied”) in which Applied announced on October 26, 2026, an increase in its strategic share ownership to approximately 20% of Besi’s outstanding shares. 
According to Applied’s press release, Applied views its investment in Besi as long-term. Applied does not intend to seek board representation at Besi, nor does it currently have plans to purchase additional shares of Besi.
Besi and Applied have collaborated together since 2020 on the development and commercialization of integrated hybrid bonding production systems for leading semiconductor manufacturers. The collaboration brings together Applied’s expertise in front-end manufacturing and Besi’s leading technologies in die placement, interconnect and assembly solutions. Recently, the companies have expanded their collaboration with Besi joining Applied’s EPIC Center as an Innovation Partner. Areas of collaboration target next-generation 3D IC scaling, logic and memory integration, the scaling of thermo-compression bonding and new die-on-wafer, die-on-die and die-on-panel integration platforms.
Richard W. Blickman, Besi’s Chief Executive Officer, commented :
“We welcome Applied’s increased strategic investment as further confirmation of Besi’s hybrid bonding and wafer-level assembly strategy. It also highlights future areas of potential collaboration between the companies targeting next generation AI and photonics systems for the industry’s leading customers.”

Applied Materials to Increase its Strategic Investment in BE Semiconductor Industries
Oct 26, 2026 at 4:30 PM EDT
PDF Version 
Applied enters into agreement to increase its investment to approximately 20 percent of outstanding shares, reinforcing the companies’ long-term strategic partnership in advanced packaging 
SANTA CLARA, Calif. , Oct. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Applied Materials, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMAT) today announced it is increasing its investment in BE Semiconductor Industries N.V. (Besi) ( Euronext Amsterdam : BESI), a leading manufacturer of assembly equipment for the semiconductor industry, to approximately 20 percent of Besi’s outstanding shares. The share purchase would add to Applied Materials’ current investment in Besi, which Applied initially made in April 2025 .
The companies have a longstanding strategic collaboration, which began in 2020 and was recently expanded with Besi joining Applied Materials’ EPIC Center as an Innovation Partner. The expanded partnership extends the companies’ co-innovation beyond hybrid bonding into new interconnect architectures and applications supporting the semiconductor industry’s AI-driven scaling roadmap. Areas of collaboration include next-generation 3D IC scaling, logic and memory integration, scaling of thermo-compression bonding and new die-on-wafer, die-on-die and die-on-panel integration platforms.
“Applied Materials is adding to its investment in Besi as hybrid bonding technology and next-generation interconnect architectures become increasingly critical enablers of energy-efficient AI compute performance,” said Dr. Prabu Raja , President of the Semiconductor Products Group at Applied Materials. “We also look forward to furthering our strategic collaboration with Besi and delivering the innovative products and technologies our customers need to scale AI systems.”
Applied Materials has entered into an accelerated share purchase agreement for the Besi shares, and the delivery of the shares is subject to the expiration or termination of the applicable waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended (the HSR Act).
Applied Materials views its investment in Besi as long term. Applied currently has no intention to increase its investment in Besi beyond approximately 20 percent, and Applied does not intend to seek board representation at Besi.
Forward-Looking Statements 
This press release contains forward-looking statements regarding the purchase of Besi shares by Applied Materials. These statements and their underlying assumptions are subject to risks and uncertainties. Factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied by such statements include the expiration or termination of the applicable waiting period under the HSR Act and the risks and uncertainties described in our filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including our most recent Forms 10-K, 10-Q and 8-K. All forward-looking statements are based on management’s current estimates, projections and assumptions, and we assume no obligation to update them.
About Applied Materials 
Applied Materials, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMAT) is the leader in materials engineering solutions that are at the foundation of virtually every new semiconductor and advanced display in the world. The technology we create is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation chips. At Applied, we push the boundaries of science and engineering to deliver material innovation that changes the world. Learn more at www.appliedmaterials.com .

title: Infineon to establish the world’s first high-volume manufacturing facility for gallium nitride power semiconductors on 300-millimeter wafers in Europe Business & Financial Press Oct 27, 2026
query: https://www.infineon.com/about/press
content_text:
Infineon to establish the world’s first high-volume manufacturing facility for gallium nitride power semiconductors on 300-millimeter wafers in Europe
Business & Financial Press
Oct 27, 2026 
Investment of around €1.1 billion in the Villach site as a global competence center for power semiconductors 
Next-generation power semiconductors to meet growing demand for energy-efficient chips, including AI data centers, energy infrastructure, e-mobility and robotics 
Ramp-up aligned with market demand 
€319 million in funding under the European Chips Act to strengthen technological sovereignty 
Munich, Germany/Vienna, Austria – 27 October 2026 – Infineon Technologies AG is establishing the world’s first high-volume manufacturing facility for next-generation gallium nitride (GaN) power semiconductors on 300-millimeter wafers in Europe. As part of the project, Infineon will invest around €1.1 billion in its existing cleanroom facilities at the Villach site by 2034. Leveraging both the existing and upgraded infrastructure will enable highly efficient and cost-effective expansion of manufacturing capacity. Production is scheduled to start by the end of 2027. Infineon’s investment addresses the rapidly growing demand for high-performance power supply solutions. Gallium nitride enables significant efficiency gains in numerous applications, such as AI data centers, energy infrastructure, e-mobility, robotics and consumer electronics.
Infineon is a leader in gallium nitride power electronics. Two years ago, Infineon achieved a technological milestone by successfully processing the world’s first 300-millimeter gallium nitride wafers. Chip production on 300-millimeter wafers is more advanced and significantly more efficient than 200-millimeter wafer production, since the larger wafer diameter yields 2.3 times as many chips per wafer. Infineon is now transferring this technology to the world’s first high-volume manufacturing facility serving customers.
“This substantial investment shows our clear commitment to strengthening the European semiconductor ecosystem and Europe’s technological sovereignty. By establishing high-volume manufacturing on 300-millimeter wafers, we will be the first company in the world to bring gallium nitride power electronics into volume production,” says Jochen Hanebeck, CEO of Infineon Technologies AG . “In doing so, we are paving the way for the widespread use of gallium nitride in a wide range of key applications in areas such as artificial intelligence, energy infrastructure, e-mobility and robotics. This new, state-of-the-art manufacturing facility translates innovation leadership into direct customer benefits.”
Christian Stocker, Federal Chancellor of the Republic of Austria: “With Infineon’s billion-euro investment, we are witnessing one of the largest single investments in the history of Austria’s high-tech industry. This is not only a strong commitment to Austria as a business location but also helps ensure that the future of the semiconductor industry will not be shaped solely in Asia or the United States, but also in Austria and Europe. Villach will thus become home to a globally unique production facility for one of the key technologies that will shape the future. This will strengthen our international competitiveness and secure jobs and value creation in Austria. After all, Austria may not be a country with unlimited natural resources, but it is a country with an unlimited wealth of talent. Our cutting-edge research sets international standards, and companies such as Infineon demonstrate every day how innovation made in Austria works. These are precisely the strengths we want to build on with our industrial strategy so that, by 2035, Austria will once again rank among the world’s top ten industrial nations.”
Wolfgang Hattmannsdorfer, Austrian Federal Minister for Economic Affairs: “Chips are as important to tomorrow’s economy as oil was to yesterday’s. Europe currently accounts for only around 10 percent of global chip production. For me, the conclusion is clear: We must also manufacture this key technology in Europe. Austria is already a leader in energy-efficient chips. Relative to our population, we rank first in the EU in business R&D spending in the semiconductor sector. With our industrial strategy, we intend to build on this lead and not only research new technologies but also manufacture them on an industrial scale. This benefits the entire economy: Statistically, every job in the chip industry can provide six additional jobs across the broader economy. That is why we intend to support Infineon’s new chip production with up to 319 million euros - subject to clear funding criteria for the location. This will ensure that public funds strengthen value creation and jobs in Austria over the long term.”
The investment in this first-of-a-kind technology is being supported under the European Chips Act. The European Commission approved €319 million in state aid. The formal funding commitment by the Austrian Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs, Energy and Tourism is expected within the stipulated time limits. By approving the funding from the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs, Energy and Tourism, the European Commission is not only enabling the expansion of manufacturing capacities in Europe but is also generating positive spillover effects in related sectors – for example, through cross-border collaboration with universities and research institutions and improved access to innovative technologies and products for start-ups and small and medium-sized enterprises.
“Competitiveness and technological sovereignty emerge where excellent research is translated into industrial value creation. This is precisely where our flagship project comes in: From Austria, we are bringing innovation into industrial application, strengthening our technological leadership and securing highly skilled jobs. Microelectronics is a key industry with enormous leverage for the economy and society. The entire Austrian semiconductor ecosystem benefits – from research organizations and universities to industrial partners. We are thus sustainably strengthening Europe’s competitiveness and strategic autonomy in microelectronics,” emphasizes Sabine Herlitschka, CEO of Infineon Technologies Austria AG. 
The investment strengthens Villach’s role as a global competence center for power electronics and new semiconductor materials. Infineon Austria currently employs around 5,800 people, approximately 4,800 of them at the Villach[1] site. Together with universities, research institutions, start-ups and industry partners, Infineon forms the core of an internationally recognized microelectronics ecosystem in southern Austria. The establishment of the new 300-millimeter GaN manufacturing facility will also create positive synergies with the power electronics research and development activities located in Villach.
Gallium nitride is an advanced semiconductor material that can switch and convert electricity much more efficiently. This enables smaller, more powerful and more energy-efficient electronic systems with lower energy loss and reduced heat generation. Analysts expect the market for GaN power semiconductors to grow to approximately USD 3.5 billion by 2031, representing annual growth of around 35 percent between 2025 and 2031.[2]
[1] Fiscal year 2025, as of September 30, 2025
[2] Yole Group: Power GaN 2026 report. https://www.yolegroup.com/product/report/power-gan-2026/ 
Images from the press briefing will be available here starting at approximately 9:15 a.m. CET: https://www.apa-fotoservice.at/galerie/40217 
About Infineon
Infineon Technologies AG is a global semiconductor leader in power systems and IoT. Infineon drives decarbonization and digitalization with its products and solutions. The Company had around 57,000 employees worldwide (end of September 2025) and generated revenue of about €14.7 billion in the 2025 fiscal year (ending 30 September). Infineon is listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (ticker symbol: IFX) and in the USA on the OTCQX International over-the-counter market (ticker symbol: IFNNY).

title: Charles River, Labcorp, and FDA Collaborate to Validate New Preclinical Methods for Abuse Potential Assessment
source: Charles River - News Releases / Press Releases

View printer-friendly version 
Charles River, Labcorp, and FDA Collaborate to Validate New Preclinical Methods for Abuse Potential Assessment
PDF Version 
Joint research effort seeks to improve abuse potential assessment tools to support drug development and public health decision-making 
WILMINGTON, Mass. --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 22, 2026--
Charles River Laboratories International, Inc. (NYSE: CRL) today announced a Research Collaboration Agreement (RCA) with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and Labcorp for developing sensitive screening tools to quantify and rank the abuse potential of new drugs, including abuse-deterrent formulations (ADFs) and emerging drugs of abuse. The agreement establishes a joint research framework to enhance objective, standardized metrics for quantifying abuse potential in preclinical models which may inform regulatory assessments of abuse potential under the Controlled Substances Act (CSA).
“Assessing abuse potential is essential for identifying risks and ensuring the safety of new drugs,” said Dr. Namandjé N. Bumpus , Chief Science and Innovation Officer, Charles River. “This collaboration will improve public health safeguards and ultimately amplify our shared efforts to protect patients and communities.”
Evaluating Abuse Potential
Abuse potential assessments are vital components of the safety evaluation of central nervous system-active compounds and are relied upon by FDA and the Drug Enforcement Administration for scheduling control measures.
Enhancing objective, reproducible methods to assess abuse potential is important for advancing regulatory science and supporting evidence-based decision-making. This collaboration will help evaluate approaches that could improve the consistency and sensitivity of abuse potential assessments, ultimately contributing to efforts to protect public health.
Charles River has extensive expertise in assessing abuse potential, having conducted over 100 abuse potential studies and contributed to assessments of the abuse potential of 15 FDA-approved products. As part of its participation in the collaboration, Charles River will leverage behavioral economic models of supply and demand to analyze self-administration data. These models assess the relative reinforcing properties of substances, helping researchers evaluate abuse potential and compare it with that of known drugs of abuse. A recent behavioral economics pilot conducted at Charles River’s Mattawan site provided preliminary proof-of-concept data that demonstrated the promise of this approach.
The collaboration aims to improve sensitivity, accuracy, and consistency across laboratories, ultimately enhancing public health by more reliably and effectively assessing the abuse potential of new drugs.
About Charles River
Charles River provides essential products and services to help pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, government agencies and leading academic institutions around the globe accelerate their research and drug development efforts. Our dedicated employees are focused on providing clients with exactly what they need to improve and expedite the discovery, early-stage development and safe manufacture of new therapies for the patients who need them. To learn more about our unique portfolio and breadth of services, visit www.criver.com .

title: Amkor Technology and NVIDIA Advance Strategic Partnership for AI Infrastructure

Amkor Technology and NVIDIA Advance Strategic Partnership for AI Infrastructure
New $1.3 billion agreement supports further expansion in South Korea , building on the companies’ recent Arizona collaboration 
TEMPE, Ariz. --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 21, 2026--
Amkor Technology, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMKR), a leading provider of outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services, today announced additional investments in South Korea for capacity expansion initiatives with NVIDIA. With this latest commitment, Amkor’s multi-year agreements with NVIDIA in Arizona and South Korea total $3 billion . The initiatives support growing demand for next-generation AI and accelerated computing platforms.
Advanced packaging technologies are essential to enabling the performance, power efficiency and integration required for next-generation computing systems. The prepayments align Amkor's manufacturing capacity with NVIDIA’s long-term growth plans and support increasing demand for advanced packaging solutions.
“Our partnership with NVIDIA underscores the critical role advanced packaging plays in enabling next-generation AI platforms,” said Kevin Engel , president and chief executive officer of Amkor Technology . “These investments build on our global manufacturing footprint and strengthen our ability to support customers through our operations in both the United States and South Korea.”
“Growing demand for accelerated computing is increasing the need for advanced packaging capacity,” said Debora Shoquist , executive vice president, operations of NVIDIA. “Our work with Amkor helps us scale production of current and next-generation platforms while strengthening the resilience of our global supply chain.”
This collaboration further strengthens Amkor’s role as a strategic manufacturing partner for NVIDIA and reinforces the companies’ shared commitment to supporting the continued expansion of AI infrastructure.
Amkor will also exhibit at NVIDIA GTC Washington, D.C. from Nov. 30 - Dec. 3 , where the company will showcase its advanced packaging and test capabilities and engage with customers, policymakers and industry leaders.
About Amkor Technology, Inc. 
Amkor Technology, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMKR) is the world’s largest U.S. headquartered OSAT and is a global leader in outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services. With a strong track record of innovation, a broad and diverse geographic footprint and solid partnerships with lead customers, Amkor delivers high-quality solutions that enable the world’s leading semiconductor and electronics companies to bring advanced technologies to market. The company’s comprehensive portfolio includes advanced packaging, wafer-level processing, and system-in-package solutions targeting applications for smartphones, data centers, artificial intelligence, automobiles and wearables. For more information visit amkor.com .

title: 3M and AWS collaborate to advance optical connectivity innovation
query: https://investors.3m.com/news-events/press-releases/rss

3M and AWS collaborate to advance optical connectivity innovation
Oct 21, 2026 • 10:28 AM EDT 
Download as PDF
AWS is investing in 3M's Expanded Beam Optical technology for its data center infrastructure 
SAINT PAUL, Minn. , Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- 3M  (NYSE: MMM) and  Amazon Web Services (AWS) today announced an expanded strategic collaboration. AWS plans to deploy and scale 3M's Expanded Beam Optical (EBO) platform for its data center infrastructure. Together, the two leading American companies will advance co-innovation and investment in optical connectivity and the critical infrastructure needed for next-generation super intelligence (SI), also known as artificial intelligence (AI). 
"AWS's adoption of 3M's EBO platform demonstrates the potential of our optical connectivity technology to meet the performance demands of next-generation data center infrastructure," said Wendy Bauer, Group President of 3M's Transportation and Electronics Business Group. "By combining AWS's infrastructure expertise and scale with 3M's innovation and materials science capabilities, we can accelerate EBO deployment, advance our transformation and strengthen U.S. innovation and investment." 
"Our work with 3M reinforces our commitment to supporting good jobs here in the U.S.," said Jens Gruenkemeir, Vice President of Supply Chain & Procurement at Amazon. "Beyond powering the services people use every day, from online banking and hospital data records to streaming entertainment and retail purchases, our data center investments are unlocking economic opportunities in the communities where we invest and across the supply chain, including the hundreds of jobs being supported by 3M as a result of its collaboration with Amazon."   
The collaboration and related investments are expected to strengthen the U.S. economy by supporting more than 500 jobs directly and indirectly, including the creation of more than 100 new roles through 2027 across Minnesota, Texas and Wisconsin. These planned roles will support customer co-innovation, technology advancement and supply chain development across 3M's optical networking portfolio and help accelerate industrywide adoption through collaboration with partners. 
3M expects to contribute nearly $0.5 billion to the U.S. economy through its optical connectivity business. This investment will accelerate innovation in optical networking and fiber termination, enable commercialization at scale and drive adoption across the data center industry.
The collaboration builds on 3M's announcement earlier this year that it will double production capacity at its Menomonie, Wisconsin, manufacturing facility, and is expected to support U.S. manufacturing partners involved in equipment and production scale-up throughout the supply chain.

title: BASF signs Letter of Intent with Taiwan’s Ministry of Economic Affairs to advance next-generation semiconductor manufacturing
query: https://www.basf.com/global/en/investors/calendar-and-publications/investor-releases
content_text:
BASF signs Letter of Intent with Taiwan’s Ministry of Economic Affairs to advance next-generation semiconductor manufacturing
Establishing new production capacity for semiconductor materials supporting chip technologies below 2 nanometers  
Expanding BASF’s Kuanyin site with a strengthened Innovation Center and advanced quality analysis capabilities  
Strengthening supply chain resilience and enhancing customer support in Taiwan and beyond  
Taipei – October 20, 2026 – BASF today signed a Letter of Intent (LOI) with Taiwan’s Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), underscoring its long-term commitment to supporting the growth of Taiwan’s semiconductor ecosystem. Through this investment, BASF’s Electronic Materials business is expanding its Kuanyin site in Taoyuan with additional production capacity for advanced semiconductor materials, enhanced quality analysis capabilities, and an expanded Innovation Center. The investment is designed to support increasing global demand for leading-edge semiconductor manufacturing technologies, including advanced nodes below 2 nanometers, while strengthening supply chain resilience and customer proximity.
“Taiwan is a global hub for semiconductor innovation and manufacturing, with leading-edge process technologies and a highly integrated industry ecosystem. Setting the strategic base for BASF’s global Electronic Materials operations in Taiwan in 2025 reflected the strategic importance of Taiwan within the global semiconductor ecosystem and reinforced our confidence in the market’s long-term growth potential,” said Gops Pillay, President, Global Operating Division of BASF.
As the semiconductor industry progresses toward process nodes below 2 nanometers, demand for advanced, high-purity specialty chemical formulations continues to rise. Through the expansion of its Kuanyin site, BASF will strengthen its Innovation Center and broaden its technical and analytical capabilities for leading-edge semiconductor technologies supporting the AI era. The investment will deepen collaboration with key industry partners, enabling the joint development of next-generation materials while reinforcing Taiwan’s position as a global semiconductor innovation hub.
The investment will further strengthen BASF’s local manufacturing, quality assurance and technical service capabilities in Taiwan, enabling the company to provide customers with a more reliable supply of advanced semiconductor materials, faster technical support, and closer collaboration. At the same time, it will enhance supply chain resilience and reinforce BASF’s role as a trusted long-term partner to the semiconductor industry.
“The signing of this Letter of Intent marks another important milestone in BASF’s long-term commitment to the semiconductor industry,” said Jens Liebermann, Senior Vice President, Global Electronic Materials business and Chairman of BASF Taiwan. “As semiconductor technologies continue to advance, innovation in materials must keep pace with our customers’ evolving needs. By strengthening our local manufacturing, innovation, and technical service capabilities, we are deepening collaboration with our customers and accelerating the development of materials solutions for future technology generations, while further enhancing supply chain resilience.”
As a trusted materials partner to the global semiconductor industry, BASF’s Electronic Materials business has maintained a strong presence in Taiwan for more than two decades. The business provides high-performance process chemicals and customized formulation solutions for the advanced semiconductor and display industry as well as specialized metal systems for consumer electronics applications. 
 
About BASF’s Dispersions & Resins division  
The Dispersions & Resins division of BASF develops, produces and markets a range of high-quality polymer dispersions, resins, additives and electronic materials worldwide. These raw materials are used in formulations for several industries, including coatings, construction, adhesives, printing and packaging, electronics and paper. With its comprehensive product portfolio and extensive knowledge of the industry, the Dispersions & Resins division offers its customers innovative and sustainable solutions and helps them advance their formulations. For further information about the Dispersions & Resins division, please visit  www.dispersions-resins.basf.com 
 
About BASF 
At BASF, we create chemistry for a sustainable future. Our ambition: We want to be the preferred chemical company to enable our customers’ green transformation. We combine economic success with environmental protection and social responsibility. Around 95,000 employees in the BASF Group contribute to the success of our customers in nearly all sectors and almost every country in the world. Our portfolio comprises, as core businesses, the segments Chemicals, Materials, Industrial Solutions, and Nutrition & Care; our standalone businesses are bundled in the segments Surface Technologies and Agricultural Solutions. BASF generated sales of around €60 billion in 2025. BASF shares are traded on the stock exchange in Frankfurt (BAS) and as American Depositary Receipts (BASFY) in the United States. Further information at  www.basf.com

Strategic and operational highlights
The following are recently announced highlights:
3M entered into an expanded strategic commercial relationship with Amazon to deploy and scale 3M's optical connectivity and other Data Center related products. 3M issued a warrant to Amazon to purchase up to 3.2 million shares of 3M common stock based upon the achievement of $6 billion in cumulative sales of optical connectivity and other Data Center related products over the next seven years, and other event-based milestones.
3M is collaborating with Genius Electronic Optical Co., Ltd. (GSEO), an optical technology company, to advance technology development and manufacturing for 3M's Expanded Beam Optics (EBO) solutions. In support of these efforts, 3M is investing to acquire ~4.7% of GSEO's common shares. The collaboration brings together 3M's EBO technology leadership, optical interconnect expertise, materials science, manufacturing scale and customer relationships with GSEO's precision optics manufacturing capabilities and production scale.
3M introduced Cooling Film technology for fleet and rail applications , expanding its portfolio of thermal management solutions for transportation customers. Applied to vehicle roofs, the highly reflective performance film uses thermal management technology to reduce heat buildup and help keep interiors noticeably cooler.
3M showcased how its materials science expertise supports innovation in golf equipment through its collaboration with PING . By pairing PING's expertise in club design and custom manufacturing with 3M's broad portfolio of materials science solutions, the two companies can collaborate on engineering solutions that turn complex technical challenges into repeatable, high-quality results on the course.
3M and BOE established a joint innovation laboratory to accelerate next-generation display technology development.  The joint research and development platform brings together BOE's display innovation and end-use application expertise with 3M's materials science capabilities to accelerate higher-performance solutions across LCD, OLED and MLED applications, including improvements in light efficiency, foldable displays and ultra-narrow bezel processes.
3M continued to expand its work with U.S. and international government customers, with third-quarter awards supporting defense, health care, and emergency response needs. Awards included PELTOR™ communication and hearing protection solutions for various U.S. military services and Scott SCBAs for the U.S. Navy, respirator and SCBA products for the National Institutes of Health, and respirators for international customers, reflecting 3M's growing work with government partners around the world.
