STRATEGIC REPORT
Chair’s statement
Strategic report
This has been a strong year for Renishaw, with
growing demand from key sectors driving record
sales and profit, despite the impact of ongoing
geopolitical uncertainty on international trade.
This success is a clear demonstration that Renishaw’s
strategy for long-term organic growth is working.
At the heart of that growth model is a strong focus on
innovation, which is helping the business to develop
more efficient, easier-to-use products that address
significant trends in our markets, while continuing
to solve specific customer challenges.
This year’s performance is also thanks to our talented
people, led by our Chief Executive Officer, Will Lee,
and his executives. The team and our people across
the world have reacted quickly to increased demand
from key markets, and shown great resilience and
agility in the face of supply chain pressures.
To do this following the cost reduction programme
at the beginning of the year is testament to their
commitment to the business, our customers and
each other, and I would like to thank everyone for
their achievements.
Continuing to evolve the Board
We made some key changes to the Board this year,
with John Shipsey appointed as our new Chief
Financial Officer and Executive Director in
April 2026, after Allen Roberts stepped down in
December 2025. The Board and I would like to
thank Allen for his exemplary 46 years at Renishaw.
Also, my thanks to Rob Macdonald, who served as
Interim Group Finance Director during this transition.
Rob has done an outstanding job during an extremely
important and busy period for Renishaw.
Also in April 2026, I was honoured to accept the role
of permanent Chair of Renishaw and retain my role
as Chair of the Nomination Committee.
In September 2025, we welcomed Camille Deer
to the Board as a Non-executive Director. Like our
other founding family Board representatives, Non-
executive Director Richard McMurtry, and Observer
Ben McMurtry, Camille has approached the role with
considerable engagement, eager learning and
openness. She has also brought fresh eyes and
excellent questions to the Board’s discussions this
year, reflecting the culture and values that our two
founders, John Deer and the late Sir David McMurtry,
instilled in the business over many years. The Board
welcomed the formation of a joint family holding
company in November 2025 and believes it gives
Renishaw a clear structure to build on David and
John’s legacy for long-term success. For more
information see page 58.
I believe the Board’s evolution over the past two years
has strengthened our leadership at a time of changing
risks and opportunities in our global markets.
An independent review of the Board, conducted
on Renishaw’s behalf by Fidelio Partners in the year,
confirms my confidence and demonstrated that we
are working well together. This review also provided
recommendations on areas for improvement, which
we discuss in more detail on pages 81 to 82.
A clearer business structure to
accelerate growth
The Board has been impressed with the executive
team’s collaborative approach to responding to the
rapid changes in customer demand this year.
While our performance reinforces the Board’s
confidence in Renishaw’s strategy for long-term
growth, we must ensure the business is agile
enough to make the most of future opportunities,
while navigating markets that can be highly cyclical.
The Board has, therefore, supported the Executive
Committee’s work to reshape Renishaw’s structure
around three segments. The Board believes these
changes provide greater clarity and enable greater
efficiency across the business.
A strong Executive Committee and clearer
reporting structure have had a positive impact
on Board discussions, with a deeper focus on
key topics, such as strategy, organisation and
productivity. The creation of the Specialised
Technologies segment has been particularly helpful,
giving the Board a much clearer view of opportunities
and challenges in new or developing businesses.
The Board has also benefited from greater
engagement with our three regional presidents,
who I’d like to thank for helping us better understand
the trends driving specific international markets.
At the beginning of the year, the Board oversaw the
implementation of a cost reduction programme.
Recognising the programme’s impact on colleagues
across the Group, the Board received regular
updates on how the business has supported our
people during this period.
2 Renishaw plc Annual Report 2026
A maturing approach to stakeholder
engagement
Our investors have welcomed Renishaw’s more
transparent reporting structure. Together with
our strengthened investor engagement programme,
which now includes in-person results presentations,
they see this transparency as a positive sign that the
business is evolving its approach to communicating
with key stakeholders.
This year we paid an interim dividend of 16.8p per
share (FY2025: 16.8p) and are proposing a final
dividend of 65.2p per share (FY2025: 61.3p),
resulting in a total dividend for the year of 82.0p per
share, a 5% increase on the previous year. In addition
to the final dividend, we have also approved a special
dividend of 70.0p per share as an interim dividend.
As well as our increasing engagement with investors,
Renishaw’s external profile is growing in other ways.
For example, this year Richard McMurtry, Will Lee
and I met with several key UK government department
officials, including through hosted site visits. These
meetings were an important opportunity to discuss
Renishaw’s role in the UK economy and industrial
strategy, as well as to demonstrate some
of our products.
It was also a pleasure to attend EMO Hannover
with the founder families in September 2025.
Held every two years, this is a huge, five-day
manufacturing technology event. It was a great
opportunity to see our industry in action and talk
to Renishaw colleagues, business partners and
customers, some of whom have worked with us for
decades. These events give the Board a unique
insight into the business, and I was particularly proud
to be a small part of the launch of our Equator-X
gauge. Since then, Equator-X has gone on to become
one of our big success stories this year (see page 16).
I’ve also enjoyed spending time with many of our
UK engineering and manufacturing teams during
the year. As Chair, and an engineer, I’m privileged
to see many of the next-generation products in
development. My particular thanks to our three
business segment directors, Louise Callanan
(Specialised Technologies), Derek Marshall (Industrial
Metrology) and Steve Oakes (Position Measurement),
for introducing me to our world-leading products,
engineers and scientists. My regular visits to our
largest manufacturing site in Miskin, Wales, have also
been exciting as volumes increased during the year,
and quality was enhanced by the use of our own
products in the production process.
STRATEGIC
REPORT
Looking ahead
It has been a pleasure to work alongside my
colleagues this year, and I believe we’re continuing
to build a Board that blends deep experience in the
business with fresh perspectives. We will need more
of both in the coming year as we implement the
recommendations of the Board review, and continue
to support and challenge the Executive Committee.
In doing so, I believe Renishaw can build on the
successes of the past year, while continuing to
navigate our customers’ changing needs and
staying alert to the challenges and opportunities
we see ahead of us.
Sir David Grant
Chair

Renishaw plc Annual Report 2026 3
STRATEGIC REPORT
Chief Executive Officer’s review
Accelerating demand in many of our markets this
year, including the semiconductor and aerospace
and defence sectors, has helped deliver strong
revenue growth across our segments and regions,
with particular progress in our emerging product
lines. This performance reflects the strength of
our strategy for long-term organic growth. It also
highlights the significant benefits of our commitment
to, and investment in, innovation to address large
structural trends, such as increasing precision in
manufacturing processes and rising industrial
automation to tackle skills shortages.
There have been challenges along the way,
with flat demand in some of our traditional markets.
Throughout, our people have shown great resilience,
while continuing to navigate geopolitical uncertainty
and increasing trade protectionism, and supporting
our cost reduction programme. This is exemplified
by our sales, service and manufacturing teams,
who responded quickly to changing customer needs.
I would like to join Sir David in thanking all our
people for their commitment this year.
Strong financial performance in FY2026
Turning to this year’s headline figures, at a Group
level, our total revenue for the year was £815.8m,
compared with £713.0m in FY2025. Revenue at
constant exchange rates*, excluding the impact
of forward contracts, increased by 17.3%.
This is our first year of reporting on our three
segments: Industrial Metrology (IM), Position
Measurement (PM) and Specialised Technologies
(ST). We saw solid growth in IM, with a substantial
proportion coming from our emerging metrology
products. In PM, we delivered strong sales growth
from our established encoder product line, and
we are seeing pleasing opportunities in our emerging
encoder products, which allow us to address
new markets.
Additive manufacturing (AM) products were the
key driver of performance improvement in ST.
As well as achieving multiple machine orders from
existing customers, we are gaining market share,
particularly in aerospace and defence. We explain
our new structure and give more performance details
in our Segment review on pages 14 to 20.
Each of our three regions had a positive year.
In APAC, revenue grew, by 17% at constant
exchange rates, to £381.9m, mainly driven by
demand for position encoders from semiconductor
and electronics manufacturing equipment builders.
The semiconductor market undergoes multi-year
business cycles, and our sales and manufacturing
teams have worked hard to capitalise on the current
AI-driven upturn. Demand was also strong in the
region for our Equator shopfloor gauging systems,
particularly from consumer electronics subcontract
manufacturers. Revenue for the Americas grew,
by 35% at constant exchange rates, to £219.0m,
led by strong demand for high-value capital
equipment sales, such as our 5-axis CMMs and
our metal AM machines. The aerospace and defence
and power generation sectors were the main drivers
here, with the automotive sector strengthening in the
second half of the year. In EMEA, revenue grew,
by 3% at constant exchange rates, to £214.9m,
with good growth in revenue for AM machines and
position encoders, while demand for IM products
was lower, especially in the automotive sector.
Adjusted* profit before tax for the year was £168.0m
(FY2025: £127.2m). Adjusted earnings per share
was 179.5p (FY2025: 137.8p). Adjusted measures are
the ones the Board uses to measure our underlying
trading performance. Statutory profit before tax was
£150.0m (FY2025: £118.0m), leading to Statutory
earnings per share of 163.5p (FY2025: 115.2p).
Read more in the Chief Financial Officer’s review
on page 21.

4 Renishaw plc Annual Report 2026
Strong strategic progress underpinned
by innovation
Everything we do at Renishaw is guided by our
purpose of Transforming Tomorrow Together and
underpinned by our strategy, which we set out on
pages 7 to 9. This year’s performance reflects
the progress we’re making against our three strategic
priorities – growing our existing markets, increasing
the value of the technology that we sell, and extending
into new, high-growth markets – as I explain below.
Our long-term commitment to innovation is a key
driver across these priorities, helping us to unlock
the opportunities that arise from the big structural
trends I mentioned earlier, and, in turn, to deliver
our strategy.
Growing in our existing markets
We saw strong growth in our existing markets this
year driven by one of the biggest trends shaping the
world around us. The exponential growth in demand
for AI processing has triggered unprecedented
demand for semiconductors. Since our encoders are
used across the semiconductor production process,
this represents a sweet spot for Renishaw because
it relies on increasing levels of precision and
automation, and we have worked hard to win more
customers that supply this market. Our established
calibration product line has also benefited from
growing demand for increasingly precise machinery.
We continue to see rising competition, particularly in
China, from rivals offering ‘good enough’ products at
attractive prices. We are responding by developing
strategies to compete in entry-level markets.
Increasing technology value
We also made strong progress against our second
strategic priority, where we aim to increase revenue
by capturing a greater proportion of the investment
made by our end-user customers. Market response
to our new Equator-X 500 gauging system has been
really positive, with significant orders secured
precisely because it addresses the common
shopfloor challenges we know customers are
grappling with.
Our innovation in software is also helping our
progress in increasing the value of the technology
we sell. We are developing solutions that make
it easier for customers to use our products, and
also make it easier for us to sell our higher-value
technology systems. For example, this year we
launched our new MODUS IM Equator software to
help Equator and Equator-X gauging system users
maximise productivity. This software is our latest
step in improving the functionality and customer
experience of our metrology systems.
In November 2025, I had the pleasure of attending
the launch of our new AM software at the Formnext
show in Frankfurt, Germany. Called LIBERTAS,
the software enables customers to precisely print
complex shapes without the need for additional
supports. The customers I spoke to at the show were
really excited about this development, many telling
me that together with our recent TEMPUS technology,
we’ve leapfrogged the competition here. Increased
interest in AM from sectors including consumer
electronics shows the potential for Renishaw to
expand into new, high-growth markets for this line,
and validates the long-term investment we’ve
made here.
We’re also seeing strong initial interest for our new
Strada Intelligent Raman Microscope. Its entirely
motorised system, significantly faster auto-alignment
capabilities, remote access options and seamless
workflows, means industrial and multi-user
laboratories can now access advanced
chemical analysis.
Extending into new markets
Our third strategic priority is to diversify into close-
adjacent markets where we have strong market
understanding and brand awareness. Our recently
launched ASTRiA inductive encoder is designed to
give precise position feedback in harsh operating
environments and is already proving popular in
a range of markets, including aerospace and
defence. This is a great example of where our
focus on R&D and a new minimum viable product
approach has helped bring a product to market
faster, allowing us to take advantage of an exciting,
sizeable opportunity that we were not previously
able to address.
Understanding and addressing
customer needs
We’re proud of the long-term relationships we’ve
built with customers over the years. It’s always
a pleasure when I get the chance to meet them,
whether visiting their factories or at the various
trade events that I attend during the year across
our three regions. Understanding our customers’
challenges is an important aspect of how we
develop the innovative solutions to address their
needs, and something that our sales and
engineering teams do throughout the year.
One of the biggest emerging conversations is
around the impact of AI. This is an area of strategic
importance to Renishaw due to our role in supporting
the manufacturing of advanced semiconductors,
and we continue to develop the next generation
of position encoders to meet the needs of this
demanding sector. AI also affects our business in
other ways, helping our people to innovate and be
more productive, while also heightening cyber risks.

Chief Executive Officer’s review continued
A simpler, more focused Renishaw
While the benefits of innovation are clear in this
year’s performance, our new structure has also
helped, with three segments that are more closely
linked to our customers and end-user markets.
As well as giving investors a better understanding
of our business, the changes support the continued
delivery of our strategy, with a single leader for
each segment accountable for every stage of
product delivery.
The new structure is having an impact on the
Executive Committee as well, with our new segment
directors, Louise Callanan (ST), Derek Marshall (IM)
and Steve Oakes (PM), bringing renewed focus to
our discussions. At the same time, our two newest
colleagues, Group Human Resources Director,
Clare Nicholls, and Chief Financial Officer,
John Shipsey, have brought fresh external
perspectives, complementing the deep expertise
of other Committee members to help plan the next
phase of our growth and innovation.
We continue to manage our business portfolio
to focus on core products. During the year we
completed the closure of the drug delivery aspect
of our neurological product line and we are
continuing to seek a new owner for the remaining
neurosurgical activities.
Responding to employee feedback
While restructuring the business has brought many
positives, I know this has not been the easiest year
for colleagues. The combination of our cost reduction
programme, followed by the rapid rise in demand for
some of our products, has created extra pressure
on our people and processes. So I am particularly
pleased that so many employees responded to our
latest engagement survey. A 78% participation rate
is good in any year, as was the 85% who responded
positively when asked if they feel proud to work
for Renishaw.
We’re addressing several key points raised in
the survey, including helping people feel better
connected to our strategy, developing clearer
career pathways, and making it easier for them to
do their job so that we can accelerate our growth.
6 Renishaw plc Annual Report 2026
Simplifying our processes to
accelerate growth
We are committed to simplifying and clarifying our
operating model – our blueprint for what we do and
how we work – while retaining what makes us special.
Our new One Renishaw initiative is focused on
developing common processes in our sales, logistics
and finance functions, supported by our new global
ERP solution, Microsoft Dynamics 365. While we
have faced challenges with deploying this system,
our dedicated team has worked incredibly hard and
has done a fantastic job supporting our customers
during the year.
Refreshing our ESG strategy
I’ve spent time this year working with colleagues
to refresh our environmental, social and governance
(ESG) strategy. The purpose of this review was to
refine our goals, remove outdated elements and
streamline our targets while retaining the ambition of
our original strategy. We explain these changes and
provide an update on our progress in our ESG review
on pages 37 to 48. We continued to make progress
against our strategy this year, most notably by
reducing the emissions intensity of the aluminium
and steel we bought in FY2026 by more than 20%
(versus FY2025), against a target of 15%.
Looking ahead
We made excellent progress in FY2026, with growth
in all three segments. We are well positioned in
attractive markets that offer substantial through-cycle
growth opportunities. Our innovation-led strategy to
deliver outperformance is also delivering results, with
significant progress in our emerging product lines.
FY2027 has started strongly as we continue to benefit
from the current upturn in demand for semiconductor
manufacturing equipment. We expect further strong
progress on revenue and profit in the year ahead.
Will Lee
Chief Executive Officer

ST. PAUL, Minn. – Oct. 20, 2026 − 3M (NYSE: MMM) today reported third-quarter results.
“We delivered another quarter of strong results, including solid sales growth, continued margin expansion, double-digit EPS growth, and robust free cash flow,” said William
Brown, 3M Chairman and CEO. “Improving productivity through structural transformation and a stronger pipeline of differentiated technologies reinforce our confidence in the
full-year outlook and long-term growth and margin potential. I want to thank the 3M team for their focus on customers and disciplined execution, which continues to strengthen
our performance and create shareholder value.”

Strategic and operational highlights

3M entered into an expanded strategic commercial relationship with Amazon to deploy and scale 3M’s optical connectivity and other Data Center related products. 3M
issued a warrant to Amazon to purchase up to 3.2 million shares of 3M common stock based upon the achievement of $6 billion in cumulative sales of optical
connectivity and other Data Center related products over the next seven years, and other event-based milestones.
3M is collaborating with Genius Electronic Optical Co., Ltd. (GSEO), an optical technology company, to advance technology development and manufacturing for
3M's Expanded Beam Optics (EBO) solutions. In support of these efforts, 3M is investing to acquire ~4.7% of GSEO's common shares. The collaboration brings
together 3M's EBO technology leadership, optical interconnect expertise, materials science, manufacturing scale and customer relationships with GSEO's precision
optics manufacturing capabilities and production scale.
3M introduced Cooling Film technology for fleet and rail applications, expanding its portfolio of thermal management solutions for transportation customers. Applied
to vehicle roofs, the highly reflective performance film uses thermal management technology to reduce heat buildup and help keep interiors noticeably cooler.
3M showcased how its materials science expertise supports innovation in golf equipment through its collaboration with PING. By pairing PING’s expertise in club
design and custom manufacturing with 3M’s broad portfolio of materials science solutions, the two companies can collaborate on engineering solutions that turn
complex technical challenges into repeatable, high-quality results on the course.
3M and BOE established a joint innovation laboratory to accelerate next-generation display technology development. The joint research and development platform
brings together BOE’s display innovation and end-use application expertise with 3M’s materials science capabilities to accelerate higher-performance solutions across
LCD, OLED and MLED applications, including improvements in light efficiency, foldable displays and ultra-narrow bezel processes.
3M continued to expand its work with U.S. and international government customers, with third-quarter awards supporting defense, health care, and emergency
response needs. Awards included PELTOR™ communication and hearing protection solutions for various U.S. military services and Scott SCBAs for the U.S. Navy,
respirator and SCBA products for the National Institutes of Health, and respirators for international customers, reflecting 3M’s growing work with government
partners around the world.
Updated full-year 2026 guidance
3M provided an update to the full-year 2026 guidance provided on July 21, 2026, incorporating the company’s performance year-to-date, the acquisition of Madison Fire &
Rescue, and a change in non-GAAP treatment of amortization.

About us
Who we are
We are a world leader in sensors and
systems for measurement and manufacturing.
Our purpose
Transforming
Tomorrow
Together
We innovate with our customers to make
the products of the future, transforming
their capabilities through unparalleled levels
of precision, productivity and practicality.
Our strategy
– Deliver innovation-led organic growth
through disciplined investment and
focused execution.
– Focus on attractive markets with durable
growth potential, enabled by long-term
customer relationships.
– Build a manufacturing technology
powerhouse by growing our market-
leading positions, scaling our emerging
product lines, and diversifying into
close-adjacent markets.
– Accelerate growth through targeted
acquisitions.
Our culture
Our founders set out to build a company that
stood apart – proudly independent, grounded
in a love of engineering and manufacturing,
with long-term thinking and never losing sight
of doing interesting, pioneering work.
This ethos is ingrained in our culture, which
is built on our values of innovation, inspiration,
integrity and involvement. These values guide
the way we behave and the decisions we
make, both as a business and as individuals.
Where we operate
We are a global business. We work closely
with our customers around the world to solve
complex engineering and science challenges
and improve their products and processes.
We have three segments: Industrial Metrology
(IM), Position Measurement (PM), and
Specialised Technologies (ST). You can find
an overview of these on pages 14 to 20.
We operate in three regions: APAC, EMEA
and the Americas. Most of our R&D and
manufacturing takes place in the UK, and
we have other major manufacturing sites
in Ireland and India.

STRATEGIC REPORT
Chair’s statement
Strategic report
This has been a strong year for Renishaw, with
growing demand from key sectors driving record
sales and profit, despite the impact of ongoing
geopolitical uncertainty on international trade.
This success is a clear demonstration that Renishaw’s
strategy for long-term organic growth is working.
At the heart of that growth model is a strong focus on
innovation, which is helping the business to develop
more efficient, easier-to-use products that address
significant trends in our markets, while continuing
to solve specific customer challenges.
This year’s performance is also thanks to our talented
people, led by our Chief Executive Officer, Will Lee,
and his executives. The team and our people across
the world have reacted quickly to increased demand
from key markets, and shown great resilience and
agility in the face of supply chain pressures.
To do this following the cost reduction programme
at the beginning of the year is testament to their
commitment to the business, our customers and
each other, and I would like to thank everyone for
their achievements.
Continuing to evolve the Board
We made some key changes to the Board this year,
with John Shipsey appointed as our new Chief
Financial Officer and Executive Director in
April 2026, after Allen Roberts stepped down in
December 2025. The Board and I would like to
thank Allen for his exemplary 46 years at Renishaw.
Also, my thanks to Rob Macdonald, who served as
Interim Group Finance Director during this transition.
Rob has done an outstanding job during an extremely
important and busy period for Renishaw.
Also in April 2026, I was honoured to accept the role
of permanent Chair of Renishaw and retain my role
as Chair of the Nomination Committee.
In September 2025, we welcomed Camille Deer
to the Board as a Non-executive Director. Like our
other founding family Board representatives, Non-
executive Director Richard McMurtry, and Observer
Ben McMurtry, Camille has approached the role with
considerable engagement, eager learning and
openness. She has also brought fresh eyes and
excellent questions to the Board’s discussions this
year, reflecting the culture and values that our two
founders, John Deer and the late Sir David McMurtry,
instilled in the business over many years. The Board
welcomed the formation of a joint family holding
company in November 2025 and believes it gives
Renishaw a clear structure to build on David and
John’s legacy for long-term success. For more
information see page 58.
I believe the Board’s evolution over the past two years
has strengthened our leadership at a time of changing
risks and opportunities in our global markets.
An independent review of the Board, conducted
on Renishaw’s behalf by Fidelio Partners in the year,
confirms my confidence and demonstrated that we
are working well together. This review also provided
recommendations on areas for improvement, which
we discuss in more detail on pages 81 to 82.
A clearer business structure to
accelerate growth
The Board has been impressed with the executive
team’s collaborative approach to responding to the
rapid changes in customer demand this year.
While our performance reinforces the Board’s
confidence in Renishaw’s strategy for long-term
growth, we must ensure the business is agile
enough to make the most of future opportunities,
while navigating markets that can be highly cyclical.
The Board has, therefore, supported the Executive
Committee’s work to reshape Renishaw’s structure
around three segments. The Board believes these
changes provide greater clarity and enable greater
efficiency across the business.
A strong Executive Committee and clearer
reporting structure have had a positive impact
on Board discussions, with a deeper focus on
key topics, such as strategy, organisation and
productivity. The creation of the Specialised
Technologies segment has been particularly helpful,
giving the Board a much clearer view of opportunities
and challenges in new or developing businesses.
The Board has also benefited from greater
engagement with our three regional presidents,
who I’d like to thank for helping us better understand
the trends driving specific international markets.
At the beginning of the year, the Board oversaw the
implementation of a cost reduction programme.
Recognising the programme’s impact on colleagues
across the Group, the Board received regular
updates on how the business has supported our
people during this period.
2 Renishaw plc Annual Report 2026
A maturing approach to stakeholder
engagement
Our investors have welcomed Renishaw’s more
transparent reporting structure. Together with
our strengthened investor engagement programme,
which now includes in-person results presentations,
they see this transparency as a positive sign that the
business is evolving its approach to communicating
with key stakeholders.
This year we paid an interim dividend of 16.8p per
share (FY2025: 16.8p) and are proposing a final
dividend of 65.2p per share (FY2025: 61.3p),
resulting in a total dividend for the year of 82.0p per
share, a 5% increase on the previous year. In addition
to the final dividend, we have also approved a special
dividend of 70.0p per share as an interim dividend.
As well as our increasing engagement with investors,
Renishaw’s external profile is growing in other ways.
For example, this year Richard McMurtry, Will Lee
and I met with several key UK government department
officials, including through hosted site visits. These
meetings were an important opportunity to discuss
Renishaw’s role in the UK economy and industrial
strategy, as well as to demonstrate some
of our products.
It was also a pleasure to attend EMO Hannover
with the founder families in September 2025.
Held every two years, this is a huge, five-day
manufacturing technology event. It was a great
opportunity to see our industry in action and talk
to Renishaw colleagues, business partners and
customers, some of whom have worked with us for
decades. These events give the Board a unique
insight into the business, and I was particularly proud
to be a small part of the launch of our Equator-X
gauge. Since then, Equator-X has gone on to become
one of our big success stories this year (see page 16).
I’ve also enjoyed spending time with many of our
UK engineering and manufacturing teams during
the year. As Chair, and an engineer, I’m privileged
to see many of the next-generation products in
development. My particular thanks to our three
business segment directors, Louise Callanan
(Specialised Technologies), Derek Marshall (Industrial
Metrology) and Steve Oakes (Position Measurement),
for introducing me to our world-leading products,
engineers and scientists. My regular visits to our
largest manufacturing site in Miskin, Wales, have also
been exciting as volumes increased during the year,
and quality was enhanced by the use of our own
products in the production process.
STRATEGIC
REPORT
Looking ahead
It has been a pleasure to work alongside my
colleagues this year, and I believe we’re continuing
to build a Board that blends deep experience in the
business with fresh perspectives. We will need more
of both in the coming year as we implement the
recommendations of the Board review, and continue
to support and challenge the Executive Committee.
In doing so, I believe Renishaw can build on the
successes of the past year, while continuing to
navigate our customers’ changing needs and
staying alert to the challenges and opportunities
we see ahead of us.

Chair

Renishaw plc Annual Report 2026 3
STRATEGIC REPORT
Chief Executive Officer’s review
Accelerating demand in many of our markets this
year, including the semiconductor and aerospace
and defence sectors, has helped deliver strong
revenue growth across our segments and regions,
with particular progress in our emerging product
lines. This performance reflects the strength of
our strategy for long-term organic growth. It also
highlights the significant benefits of our commitment
to, and investment in, innovation to address large
structural trends, such as increasing precision in
manufacturing processes and rising industrial
automation to tackle skills shortages.
There have been challenges along the way,
with flat demand in some of our traditional markets.
Throughout, our people have shown great resilience,
while continuing to navigate geopolitical uncertainty
and increasing trade protectionism, and supporting
our cost reduction programme. This is exemplified
by our sales, service and manufacturing teams,
who responded quickly to changing customer needs.
I would like to join Sir David in thanking all our
people for their commitment this year.
Strong financial performance in FY2026
Turning to this year’s headline figures, at a Group
level, our total revenue for the year was £815.8m,
compared with £713.0m in FY2025. Revenue at
constant exchange rates*, excluding the impact
of forward contracts, increased by 17.3%.
This is our first year of reporting on our three
segments: Industrial Metrology (IM), Position
Measurement (PM) and Specialised Technologies
(ST). We saw solid growth in IM, with a substantial
proportion coming from our emerging metrology
products. In PM, we delivered strong sales growth
from our established encoder product line, and
we are seeing pleasing opportunities in our emerging
encoder products, which allow us to address
new markets.
Additive manufacturing (AM) products were the
key driver of performance improvement in ST.
As well as achieving multiple machine orders from
existing customers, we are gaining market share,
particularly in aerospace and defence. We explain
our new structure and give more performance details
in our Segment review on pages 14 to 20.
Each of our three regions had a positive year.
In APAC, revenue grew, by 17% at constant
exchange rates, to £381.9m, mainly driven by
demand for position encoders from semiconductor
and electronics manufacturing equipment builders.
The semiconductor market undergoes multi-year
business cycles, and our sales and manufacturing
teams have worked hard to capitalise on the current
AI-driven upturn. Demand was also strong in the
region for our Equator shopfloor gauging systems,
particularly from consumer electronics subcontract
manufacturers. Revenue for the Americas grew,
by 35% at constant exchange rates, to £219.0m,
led by strong demand for high-value capital
equipment sales, such as our 5-axis CMMs and
our metal AM machines. The aerospace and defence
and power generation sectors were the main drivers
here, with the automotive sector strengthening in the
second half of the year. In EMEA, revenue grew,
by 3% at constant exchange rates, to £214.9m,
with good growth in revenue for AM machines and
position encoders, while demand for IM products
was lower, especially in the automotive sector.
Adjusted* profit before tax for the year was £168.0m
(FY2025: £127.2m). Adjusted earnings per share
was 179.5p (FY2025: 137.8p). Adjusted measures are
the ones the Board uses to measure our underlying
trading performance. Statutory profit before tax was
£150.0m (FY2025: £118.0m), leading to Statutory
earnings per share of 163.5p (FY2025: 115.2p).

4 Renishaw plc Annual Report 2026
Strong strategic progress underpinned
by innovation
Everything we do at Renishaw is guided by our
purpose of Transforming Tomorrow Together and
underpinned by our strategy, which we set out on
pages 7 to 9. This year’s performance reflects
the progress we’re making against our three strategic
priorities – growing our existing markets, increasing
the value of the technology that we sell, and extending
into new, high-growth markets – as I explain below.
Our long-term commitment to innovation is a key
driver across these priorities, helping us to unlock
the opportunities that arise from the big structural
trends I mentioned earlier, and, in turn, to deliver
our strategy.
Growing in our existing markets
We saw strong growth in our existing markets this
year driven by one of the biggest trends shaping the
world around us. The exponential growth in demand
for AI processing has triggered unprecedented
demand for semiconductors. Since our encoders are
used across the semiconductor production process,
this represents a sweet spot for Renishaw because
it relies on increasing levels of precision and
automation, and we have worked hard to win more
customers that supply this market. Our established
calibration product line has also benefited from
growing demand for increasingly precise machinery.
We continue to see rising competition, particularly in
China, from rivals offering ‘good enough’ products at
attractive prices. We are responding by developing
strategies to compete in entry-level markets.
Increasing technology value
We also made strong progress against our second
strategic priority, where we aim to increase revenue
by capturing a greater proportion of the investment
made by our end-user customers. Market response
to our new Equator-X 500 gauging system has been
really positive, with significant orders secured
precisely because it addresses the common
shopfloor challenges we know customers are
grappling with.
Our innovation in software is also helping our
progress in increasing the value of the technology
we sell. We are developing solutions that make
it easier for customers to use our products, and
also make it easier for us to sell our higher-value
technology systems. For example, this year we
launched our new MODUS IM Equator software to
help Equator and Equator-X gauging system users
maximise productivity. This software is our latest
step in improving the functionality and customer
experience of our metrology systems.
In November 2025, I had the pleasure of attending
the launch of our new AM software at the Formnext
show in Frankfurt, Germany. Called LIBERTAS,
the software enables customers to precisely print
complex shapes without the need for additional
supports. The customers I spoke to at the show were
really excited about this development, many telling
me that together with our recent TEMPUS technology,
we’ve leapfrogged the competition here. Increased
interest in AM from sectors including consumer
electronics shows the potential for Renishaw to
expand into new, high-growth markets for this line,
and validates the long-term investment we’ve
made here.
We’re also seeing strong initial interest for our new
Strada Intelligent Raman Microscope. Its entirely
motorised system, significantly faster auto-alignment
capabilities, remote access options and seamless
workflows, means industrial and multi-user
laboratories can now access advanced
chemical analysis.
Extending into new markets
Our third strategic priority is to diversify into close-
adjacent markets where we have strong market
understanding and brand awareness. Our recently
launched ASTRiA inductive encoder is designed to
give precise position feedback in harsh operating
environments and is already proving popular in
a range of markets, including aerospace and
defence. This is a great example of where our
focus on R&D and a new minimum viable product
approach has helped bring a product to market
faster, allowing us to take advantage of an exciting,
sizeable opportunity that we were not previously
able to address.
Understanding and addressing
customer needs
We’re proud of the long-term relationships we’ve
built with customers over the years. It’s always
a pleasure when I get the chance to meet them,
whether visiting their factories or at the various
trade events that I attend during the year across
our three regions. Understanding our customers’
challenges is an important aspect of how we
develop the innovative solutions to address their
needs, and something that our sales and
engineering teams do throughout the year.
One of the biggest emerging conversations is
around the impact of AI. This is an area of strategic
importance to Renishaw due to our role in supporting
the manufacturing of advanced semiconductors,
and we continue to develop the next generation
of position encoders to meet the needs of this
demanding sector. AI also affects our business in
other ways, helping our people to innovate and be
more productive, while also heightening cyber risks.

A simpler, more focused Renishaw
While the benefits of innovation are clear in this
year’s performance, our new structure has also
helped, with three segments that are more closely

As well as giving investors a better understanding

We’re addressing several key points raised in

career pathways, and making it easier for them to
do their job so that we can accelerate our growth.

We are committed to simplifying and clarifying our
operating model – our blueprint for what we do and

Our new One Renishaw initiative is focused on
developing common processes in our sales, logistics

Refreshing our ESG strategy

to refresh our environmental, social and governance

refine our goals, remove outdated elements and
streamline our targets while retaining the ambition of

attractive markets that offer substantial through-cycle

significant progress in our emerging product lines.

content_text:
Jenoptik : reports order intake and profitability at record levels for the first nine months of 2026 
Published on 11/10/2026
at 01:47 am EST
Publicnow
Add MarketScreener to your sources
Share
JENOPTIK AG +4.19% 
Order intake dynamics remain very strong, particularly in the OEM businesses
Strong demand translates into revenue growth; profitability improved significantly
Full-year EBITDA margin now expected at around 22 percent
"In the first three quarters, we saw particularly strong demand, especially in our OEM businesses, which is now also reflected in our revenue and earnings performance. With a firm focus on our customers' requirements, we are concentrating our operational efforts on further improving our delivery capabilities and expanding our capacities," said Dr. Dominic Dorfner, CEO of JENOPTIK AG. "2026 will be a successful year for Jenoptik, as, amongst other things, our EBITDA margin guidance upgrade to around 22 percent at the end of October has shown. We are also very confident about 2027, given our high order backlog," commented Dr. Prisca Havranek-Kosicek, CFO of JENOPTIK AG.
Revenue growth picks up significantly
The photonics group Jenoptik achieved revenue of 803.8 million euros in the first nine months of 2026, representing an increase of 6.7 percent compared with the same period last year (prior year: 753.2 million euros). Third quarter dynamics were particularly strong, with revenue up by 18.0 percent year-over-year.
The Strategic Business Unit (SBU) Semiconductor & Advanced Manufacturing recorded revenue of 367.4 million euros in the reporting period, 16.7 percent above prior year (314.9 million euros), driven by stronger business with customers in both the lithography and inspection areas of the semiconductor equipment industry.
The SBU Biophotonics generated significantly higher revenues in the defense sector during the reporting period, while the very strong prior-year revenue base could not be reached in the medical technology business, as expected. Consequently, revenue of the SBU Biophotonics of 180.1 million euros was slightly down by 1.1 percent on the prior year's figure of 182.1 million euros.
The SBU Metrology & Production Solutions recorded revenue of 130.9 million euros in the first nine months (prior year: 139.0 million euros), which was lower across all areas, amongst other things, due to the continuing difficult market situation in the automotive industry.
The SBU Smart Mobility Solutions increased its revenue by 11.8 percent to 105.6 million euros (prior year: 94.4 million euros) driven by a strong performance in almost all regions.
Profitability reaches record level
The Group's EBITDA improved significantly in the first nine months of 2026 to 178.2 million euros, an increase of 35.2 percent compared with the prior year's figure of 131.8 million euros. Performance in the reporting period was mainly driven, besides revenue growth, by a very favorable product mix - particularly in the third quarter - and the cost-cutting measures implemented in 2025. Accordingly, the Group's EBITDA margin improved significantly to 22.2 percent in the reporting period (prior year: 17.5 percent).
Group earnings after tax were up by around 57 percent to 74.0 million euros (prior year: 47.0 million euros). Earnings per share amounted to 1.28 euros (prior year: 0.80 euros).
Order intake remained very strong, particularly in the OEM businesses
The Group's order intake improved significantly in the first nine months of 2026, rising by 41.4 percent to 1,099.2 million euros (prior year: 777.3 million euros), primarily due to strong momentum in the OEM businesses. Hence, order intake of the SBU Semiconductor & Advanced Manufacturing was up by around 90 percent (including a major order as reported in the first quarter) due to strong demand in both the lithography and inspection businesses.
The SBU Biophotonics also recorded a higher order intake (up by around 11 percent), driven by the medical technology & life sciences sector. It includes, however, a major multi-year medical technology contract in the low double-digit million-euro range in the second quarter.
The Group's book-to-bill ratio came in at 1.37 during the reporting period (prior year: 1.03). As a result, the order backlog increased to 903.2 million euros (31/12/2025: 590.8 million euros).
Investments amounted to 31.9 million euros and primarily related to technical equipment and machinery. This represents a significant decline compared to prior year's figure of 58.3 million euros, which still included investments in the new factory in Dresden.
Solid position in terms of finances and balance sheet
Free cash flow before interest and taxes improved to 114.6 million euros in the reporting period (prior year: 84.6 million euros), despite an increase in working capital tied up due to higher demand.
With an equity ratio of 59.0 percent (31/12/2025: 60.2 percent), net debt of 260.1 million euros (31/12/2025: 317.4 million euros) and a leverage ratio (net debt to EBITDA) of 1.1x (31/12/2025: 1.6x), Jenoptik maintained very sound financial and balance sheet ratios.
Full-year EBITDA margin now expected at around 22 percent
Based on the very strong order intake and order backlog, the Executive Board continues to expect to achieve revenue growth of between 5 and 9 percent year-on-year in 2026 (2025: 1,046.0 million euros).
In view of a significantly improved product mix, the Executive Board now expects an EBITDA margin of around 22 percent for the full fiscal year 2026 (previously 20 to 21 percent / 2025: 18.4 percent).
With regard to capital expenditure, following a marked decline in the first nine months, the Executive Board expects this to remain significantly below the prior year's level of 77.4 million euros for the full year (previously: slight decline). Plans to significantly expand optical production capacity, particularly at the Jena site, remain unchanged.
This forecast is subject to the political and economic conditions not deteriorating. Possible changes to the portfolio are not taken into account in this forecast.

Joby and Archer Both Turn to Defense Acquisitions as eVTOL Commercialization Timelines Remain Uncertain
Why It Matters Both leading eVTOL developers are seeking defense revenue as civil certification timelines stay uncertain and consumer eVTOL economics remain unproven, signaling that near-term commercial income is thin.
Oct 31 Disclaimer Nai500 Save 
Joby Aviation and Archer Aviation, two front-runners in the electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) industry, are pivoting toward defense acquisitions as commercial certification timelines remain uncertain and consumer-market economics are unproven.
In August, Joby said it remains on track to acquire defense specialist Resonant Sciences in a $500 million all-cash deal, alongside plans to raise $750 million by selling new common stock. Archer disclosed an agreement to acquire three subsidiaries from Boeing: autonomous eVTOL developer Wisk Aero, air-traffic-management software provider SkyGrid, and drone specialist Insitu. Upon closing, Boeing will hold approximately 16.5% of Archer after accounting for the new shares issued to fund the transaction.
For Archer, the defense push carries greater urgency. The company lags in commercial readiness and faces unresolved technical and regulatory milestones. Archer says it is ahead of Joby in securing Federal Aviation Administration approval, but Joby's completion of type inspection authorization for production-ready aircraft has complicated comparisons. Recent Midnight flights around San Francisco used conventional runway takeoff rather than vertical takeoff transitioning to horizontal flight, and the timeline for a piloted transition flight remains unclear.
Joby also has reason to pursue defense revenue, since civil eVTOL approval could take longer than investors expect and consumer eVTOL services are untested. Both companies have formed manufacturing partnerships with major automakers. Joby trades at a forward price-to-sales ratio of roughly 38, versus about 200.5 for Archer. Neither is growing revenue organically: Joby's top line this year is driven largely by its acquisition of helicopter operator Blade, while Archer's revenue comes primarily from its purchase of Hawthorne Airport in the Los Angeles area.

Rio Tinto Opens Two Argentine Lithium Projects Worth US$1.4 Billion
Written by Giann Liguid 
| 
Edited by 
Georgia Williams
Oct. 29, 2026 11:46AM PST
The company plans to invest approximately US$4 billion in growth capital across its Argentine lithium operations and expects to spend around 70 percent of it with local suppliers.
Tigarto / Adobe Stock 
Rio Tinto (ASX:RIO,NYSE:RIO,LSE:RIO) opened two lithium operations in Argentina's Catamarca province on Thursday (October 29), which is touted to add 25,000 metric tons of annual lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE) capacity once fully ramped up. 
To date, Rio Tinto has invested roughly US$1.4 billion in the Fénix 1B expansion and the new Sal de Vida operation. Both reached first production ahead of plan in the second quarter and are now ramping up.
Fénix began operating in 1997 as Argentina's first commercial lithium operation. The 1B expansion adds 10,000 metric tons of annual LCE capacity there, which raises the operation's total target to about 40,000 metric tons. Sal de Vida sits roughly 20 kilometers northeast of Fénix and targets 15,000 metric tons a year.
CEO Simon Trott linked the two projects to Rio Tinto's global target of 200,000 metric tons of annual LCE production capacity by 2028.
"Our focus now is on safely ramping up production, delivering reliable, high-quality lithium to our customers, and creating lasting value for our shareholders and Argentina," Trott said.
In Salta, Rio Tinto is building the US$2.5 billion Rincon project, which targets approximately 60,000 metric tons of annual battery-grade lithium carbonate capacity. 
In March, the company secured a US$1.175 billion financing package for Rincon from four lenders. 
Construction at Rincon started in 2025. Rio Tinto expects first production in 2028, followed by a three-year ramp-up to full capacity running across an expected lifespan of 40 years.
Outside Argentina, Rio Tinto took majority control of Nemaska Lithium (TSX:NMX) in Québec in February this year with a 53.9 percent stake and assumed direct management of the company. The Québec government holds the remaining 46.1 percent through Investissement Québec.
Rio Tinto said it plans to invest more than US$300 million in its Québec lithium business this year.

Rio Tinto Opens Two Argentine Lithium Projects Backed by $1.4 Billion
Rio Tinto has launched two lithium ventures in Argentina, underpinned by a total commitment of $1.4 billion, as the mining group accelerates its push into battery metals. The Fénix 1B expansion and the Sal de Vida operation, both located in Catamarca province, commenced first production during the second quarter of 2026, ahead of schedule, and are currently increasing output.
Once running at full capacity, the pair will contribute 25,000 tonnes of yearly lithium carbonate equivalent capacity, according to the company. At an inauguration event attended by President Javier Milei and Catamarca Governor Raúl Jalil, Rio Tinto chief executive Simon Trott said the developments draw on almost thirty years of lithium output in the province and the skills of the firm's Argentine employees. He also referenced the company's worldwide ambition of reaching 200,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent annual capacity by 2028.
Project Details
The $530-million Fénix 1B expansion contributes 10,000 tonnes of yearly capacity, raising the site's overall target to about 40,000 tonnes. Fénix started producing in 1997, becoming Argentina's first commercial lithium operation. Rio Tinto is evaluating a further expansion, with an investment decision anticipated in 2028 or 2029.
Sal de Vida, a new lithium carbonate facility situated roughly 20 km northeast of Fénix, is designed for 15,000 tonnes per year. Its initial phase required an investment of $374 million.
Both operations belong to an integrated production hub in the Salar del Hombre Muerto, whose combined resource base stands at approximately 19 million tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent. Running the sites jointly enables infrastructure sharing, efficiency gains and efforts to lower water use. Fénix employs direct lithium extraction, whereas Sal de Vida uses conventional evaporation ponds.
Counting Fénix, Sal de Vida and Olaroz, Rio Tinto's nominal lithium capacity in Argentina totals roughly 100,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent per year. Its wider Argentine holdings include a 66.5% interest in Olaroz and complete ownership of the Rincón project, which extends across Catamarca, Jujuy and Salta provinces.
Market Context
Argentina is projected to generate around 172,700 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent in 2026, a 48% rise over the prior year and over five times the 2018 figure. Between January and August 2026, lithium exports brought in $1.467 billion, up 190.5% compared with the same period twelve months earlier.
Rio Tinto intends to direct close to 70% of its planned $4 billion in Argentine lithium growth capital toward local suppliers. The spending dovetails with Milei's push to draw foreign investment via market-friendly reforms and the Large Investment Incentive Regime, which grants tax, legal and foreign-exchange advantages for 30 years to eligible projects exceeding $200 million in value.
Benchmark Mineral Intelligence projects worldwide lithium demand climbing from 2 million tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent in 2026 to 7 million tonnes by 2050, chiefly on electric vehicle and energy storage growth. Argentina's Mining Secretariat anticipates the country may surpass Chile in lithium output by 2029 and achieve yearly production of 573,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent by 2035.

SCHOTT Poonawalla Renamed SCHOTT Pharma India, Reaffirms Long-Term Commitment to Indian Pharma Market 
Written By : sheeba farhat Published On 2026-10-29T15:46:32+05:30   |   Updated On 29 Oct 2026 3:46 PM IST 
New Delhi: SCHOTT Poonawalla Private Limited will become SCHOTT Pharma India Private Limited, marking an important new chapter in the company's journey and strengthening its connection with the global SCHOTT Pharma organization.
The new identity more clearly reflects the India business’s place within SCHOTT Pharma’s global network and its role in advancing high-quality drug containment and delivery solutions for the pharmaceutical and biotech industries. It brings together the company’s strong manufacturing footprint, long-standing customer relationships and deep market expertise in India with SCHOTT Pharma’s global capabilities, innovation and scientific excellence.
For customers, partners and employees, this is a change in name, not a change in commitment. There is no change in ownership, management, employees, business strategy, operations, products, services or existing customer commitments.
The transition reinforces SCHOTT Pharma India’s long-term commitment to customers in India and international markets, while creating a stronger and more consistent connection to the global SCHOTT Pharma brand.
Building on a heritage of more than 140 years, the new identity brings the company’s heritage and future ambition under one global name, reflecting the values that continue to define SCHOTT Pharma: innovation, quality, scientific excellence and trust.
Also Read: TPG to acquire 35% stake in SCHOTT Poonawalla from SII 
SCHOTT Pharma India represents both continuity and progress: the same trusted business, capabilities and relationships, now with an identity that more clearly reflects who we are today and where we are headed.
Roy Joseph, CEO & Managing Director, SCHOTT Pharma India Private Limited, said, “SCHOTT Pharma India represents the next chapter of our journey, combining our strength in India with SCHOTT Pharma’s global innovation and expertise. We see significant opportunity to build on our capabilities, deepen collaboration with pharmaceutical and biotechnology partners, and advance drug containment and delivery solutions. As we move forward, our focus remains on growing with our customers and contributing to the safe and reliable delivery of critical therapies to patients worldwide.”
“SCHOTT Pharma India plays a critical role in patient care. With more than 3 billion containers produced annually, this company enables around 7,000 injections to reach patients every minute,” said Dr. Christian Mias, CEO of SCHOTT Pharma AG & Co. KGaA, SCHOTT Pharma India’s major shareholder. “The name change from SCHOTT Poonawalla to SCHOTT Pharma India reinforces our strategic partnership and confirms our long-term commitment to India as a key pharma hub.”
The new identity builds on the company’s strong foundation in India. During the COVID-19 pandemic, its pharmaceutical vials supported more than 4.3 billion vaccine doses worldwide, including 3 billion doses in India. As India’s only manufacturer of glass pre-fillable syringes and sterile formats, the company also strengthens local supply capabilities. Furthermore, the company continues to invest significantly towards manufacturing capacity expansions of pre-fillable syringes and cartridges, strengthening their ability to support the rapidly evolving needs of biologics, biosimilars, GLP-1 based treatments and other advanced injectable therapies.
Looking ahead, SCHOTT Pharma India will focus on expanding capabilities across pharmaceutical drug containment and drug delivery solutions, driving innovation through closer customer collaboration, and strengthening operational excellence and sustainability. These priorities will support the company as it responds to the evolving needs of pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies while contributing to India’s growing role in the global pharmaceutical value chain.
SCHOTT Pharma India is a manufacturer of advanced drug containment and delivery solutions, serving pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies across global markets. Based on innovation in specialty glass and advanced materials, the company offers a comprehensive portfolio of injectable drug containment and delivery products, including vials, cartridges, syringes and ampoules. Manufactured to stringent international quality standards, SCHOTT Pharma India’s solutions enable safe storage of vaccines and biologics. Through continued investment in innovation and operational excellence, and a strong focus on quality, reliability and customer partnership, the company addresses evolving healthcare needs and supports better patient outcomes worldwide.

What NXP Semiconductors (NXPI) Said on Its Q3 Earnings Call
4 min read 
NXPI 
Why NXP Semiconductors Could Be the AI Stock Everyone Is Missing 
NXP Semiconductors NXPI reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $3.79 billion, up 19% from a year earlier and 8% sequentially, as automotive, industrial and data-center-related demand supported growth across its business. Revenue increased 22% year over year excluding the MEMS sensor business. 
President and CEO Rafael Sotomayor said every region posted double-digit year-over-year growth. Automotive and industrial, which together represent roughly one-third of company revenue, were key contributors, alongside continued strength in data-center infrastructure. 
These 3 AI Stocks Just Crushed Earnings: Still Time To Buy? 
Non-GAAP operating margin rose 330 basis points from a year earlier to 37.1%, while non-GAAP earnings per share increased 35% to $4.20. The company generated $1.21 billion in free cash flow during the quarter, equal to approximately 32% of revenue. 
Automotive crosses $2 billion 
Automotive revenue surpassed $2 billion for the first time in the quarter. Revenue in the segment was up 17% year over year excluding sensors, driven by content gains in software-defined vehicle, or SDV, products despite what Sotomayor described as a “flattish” vehicle-production environment. 
Why NXP Semiconductors’ Post-Earnings Dip Could Be a Buying Window 
NXP said SDV revenue was running at an annualized rate above $1.5 billion in the third quarter and remains on track to reach its $2 billion target in 2027. The company expects the transition from domain-based vehicle architectures to zonal and centralized computing to increase semiconductor content per vehicle by two to three times compared with current architectures. 
The company plans to begin shipping its next-generation SDV processors, including the S32K5 zonal and S32N central-compute platforms, in 2027. Sotomayor said RV Tech, the Volkswagen-Rivian joint venture, had standardized its zonal platform on NXP’s S32K5 across both companies. NXP also expects its first S32K5 shipments in China as early as the first quarter of 2027. 
During the quarter, NXP secured its first S32K5 design win in humanoid robotics with what Sotomayor described as a leading U.S. global technology company. He said the same components used in software-defined vehicles—including central compute, sensing, networking and secure control—are moving into robotics and other intelligent edge systems. 
In response to analyst questions, management said it had not seen broad-based automotive restocking. Sotomayor said customer visibility had improved as lead times extended and automakers became more directly involved in providing demand guidance. CFO Bill Betz added that NXP serves about 40% of automotive distribution directly, giving the company close visibility into that channel. 
Industrial and data center momentum 
Industrial and IoT revenue was $802 million, up 39% from a year earlier. The industrial portion of the business grew nearly 50%, led by data centers, factory automation and healthcare, and now accounts for about 70% of industrial IoT revenue, according to the company. 
NXP said AI-enabled processors are expected to represent approximately 15% of industrial IoT processor revenue in 2026, more than double the prior year’s level. Its Ara discrete neural processing unit is gaining traction in industrial automation and automotive AI applications, with volume production anticipated in 2028. 
Communication infrastructure and other revenue rose 54% year over year to $503 million, supported by data-center and secure-card demand. NXP now expects its data-center revenue to exceed the more than $500 million outlook it previously gave for 2026 and to surpass $1 billion in a couple of years. 
Sotomayor said NXP is focused on the data-center control plane, including top-of-rack switches, controllers, processors, secure elements and interfaces. The company views networking, security and processing requirements as increasing alongside higher-performance data-center infrastructure. 
Mobile revenue was $411 million, down 4% from a year earlier. 
Margins, cash returns and fourth-quarter outlook 
Third-quarter non-GAAP gross margin was 58.6%, up 160 basis points year over year, reflecting improved factory utilization and revenue growth, Betz said. The company ended the period with $3.94 billion in cash and $10.98 billion in debt, resulting in a net leverage ratio of 1.3 times. 
Inventory days declined to 148 from 156 in the second quarter, including about 13 days of pre-built inventory associated with planned front-end factory consolidations. NXP expects to have about 15 days of pre-built inventory at the end of 2026. 
The board authorized an additional $5 billion for share repurchases, bringing total authorization to approximately $6.3 billion. NXP returned $1.7 billion to shareholders through dividends and buybacks over the trailing 12 months and said it plans to accelerate repurchases in the fourth quarter and in 2027. 
For the fourth quarter, NXP forecast revenue of $3.85 billion, plus or minus $100 million, representing growth of 15% year over year and 2% sequentially. The outlook implies 18% annual growth excluding the MEMS sensor business. 
Automotive revenue is expected to rise in the low-double-digit percentage range year over year and low-single digits sequentially. 
Industrial and IoT revenue is projected to increase in the high-20% range from a year earlier. 
Mobile revenue is expected to decline in the mid-teens percentage range year over year. 
Communication infrastructure and other revenue is forecast to rise more than 50% year over year. 
NXP expects fourth-quarter non-GAAP gross margin of 59%, plus or minus 50 basis points, and non-GAAP operating margin of 37.5% at the midpoint. It forecast non-GAAP earnings per share of $4.36 at the midpoint, up 30% year over year. 
Looking into 2027, Betz said the company expects to continue delivering double-digit revenue growth, expand gross margin to 60%, and increase capital expenditures to about 5% of revenue as it adds back-end capacity and develops a new assembly and test facility in Malaysia for production in 2028. NXP also plans to realign its end-market revenue reporting beginning in 2027 and will host an investor day on March 3 in Boston.

A long-term shareholder who rules out any governance ambitions
BE Semiconductor Industries (Besi) took note, on October 27, 2026, of a press release published the previous day by Applied Materials. In this statement, Applied announced that it had increased its strategic stake in the Dutch semiconductor assembly equipment manufacturer. According to the press release, Applied concluded an agreement intended to raise its stake to approximately 20% of Besi's outstanding shares, whose headquarters are located in Duiven, Netherlands.
Applied accompanied this announcement with three clarifications that frame its position. The group considers its investment in Besi as a long-term commitment. It does not intend to seek board representation in the company. It currently has no plans to acquire additional shares.
These statements have concrete significance for reading the shareholding structure. A stake expected to reach approximately one-fifth of the capital would make Applied Materials a significant shareholder in Besi's ownership structure. By forgoing a board seat and indicating it does not wish to increase further, Applied presents itself as a stable shareholder rather than as a player seeking to influence Besi's decisions.
Besi's press release reiterates these elements by explicitly citing Applied's statement as a source. Besi's ordinary shares are listed on Euronext Amsterdam under the symbol BESI, while its depositary receipts (Level 1 ADR) are traded on over-the-counter American markets under the symbol BESIY. Applied's new position therefore concerns a group whose value is tracked in both Europe and the United States.

The capital link is supported by an established industrial partnership. Besi and Applied have been working together since 2020 on the development and commercialization of integrated hybrid bonding production systems, intended for leading semiconductor manufacturers. This collaboration combines Applied's expertise in wafer-level chip manufacturing, upstream in the supply chain, with Besi's technologies in chip placement, interconnection, and assembly.
The partnership was recently expanded. Besi joined Applied's EPIC Center as an innovation partner. The joint work focuses on the next generation of three-dimensional integrated circuits, the integration of logic and memory, the scaling up of thermocompression bonding, as well as new wafer-to-wafer, chip-to-chip, and chip-to-panel assembly platforms.
Besi's Chief Executive Officer, Richard W. Blickman, welcomed this decision favorably. "We welcome Applied's increased strategic investment as further confirmation of Besi's strategy in hybrid bonding and wafer-level assembly," he stated, according to a translation of the press release. He added that the transaction highlights future areas of potential collaboration between the two companies, targeting next-generation artificial intelligence and photonics systems for leading customers in the industry.
An announcement following quarterly results publication and share price decline
This capital increase comes a few days after the publication of third-quarter results. On October 22, 2026, Besi reported revenue up 113.6% and quarterly net income of €107.2 million. Earnings per share came in at €1.33, against an average expectation of €1.30 from analysts, with the fourth quarter expected to remain stable.
On the market, the share has experienced a sharp decline in recent weeks. On October 15, 2026, the stock showed a decline close to 35% over one quarter. On October 23, 2026, it fell below its 150-day low, at €155.55, as several brokers, including JP Morgan and BofA, had lowered their price targets during the month.

content_text:
Applied Materials Raises BE Semiconductor Stake to 20%, Deepening AI Advanced Packaging Push; Deal Awaits U.S. Antitrust Review
Add preferred source 2 
Applied Materials announced it will raise its stake in Dutch packaging equipment maker BE Semiconductor Industries from 9% to approximately 20%, having signed an accelerated share purchase agreement, with the deal still pending U.S. antitrust review. Applied Materials became BE Semiconductor's largest shareholder after first taking a stake in April 2025, and the increased holding is aimed at AI chip advanced packaging. The two companies have collaborated on hybrid bonding technology since 2020 and have jointly developed the Kinex integrated die-to-wafer system. Applied Materials said it does not intend to push its stake above 20% or seek board seats. BE Semiconductor holds roughly 70% of the global hybrid bonding equipment market, with third-quarter orders up 96% year over year, and hybrid bonding equipment orders in the first nine months of 2026 already more than double the full-year 2025 level.
Key Elements 
Applied Materials BE Semiconductor Industries hybrid bonding EPIC Center Prabh Raja ASML Kinex Piotech 
U.S. semiconductor equipment giant Applied Materials announced Monday that it will raise its stake in Dutch packaging equipment maker BE Semiconductor Industries (BESI) from the current 9% to approximately 20%, deepening cooperation between the two companies in advanced packaging for artificial intelligence (AI) chips. The increased holding has been signed under an accelerated share purchase agreement but still requires U.S. antitrust review.
Applied Materials became the largest shareholder of the Dutch company after first taking a 9% stake in April 2025. At that time, BE Semiconductor had a market value of about $13 billion. Under the plan, the stake will approach 20% once the increase is completed. However, Applied Materials made clear that at this stage it does not intend to push its holding above 20% or seek seats on BE Semiconductor's board, indicating that this is a long-term strategic investment centered on technology cooperation rather than a move toward a full acquisition.
The expanded cooperation focuses on next-generation chip interconnection and packaging technology, with the goal of supporting the next generation of AI semiconductors. The two companies have jointly invested in hybrid bonding process development since 2020, a technology regarded as a key link in advanced packaging and mainly used for high-performance chips.
Hybrid bonding is characterized by directly bonding copper interconnects and dielectric layers without the need for traditional bumps, allowing a substantial increase in connection density between chips. The two companies have jointly developed the Kinex integrated die-to-wafer hybrid bonding system, combining Applied Materials' expertise in etching, planarization, deposition and inspection with BE Semiconductor's technology in high-precision die placement and assembly. BE Semiconductor also recently formally joined Applied Materials' newly established chip equipment research organization, the EPIC Center.
Prabh Raja, president of Applied Materials' Semiconductor Products Group, said in a statement: "We look forward to further deepening our strategic collaboration with Besi to deliver the innovative products and technologies customers need to scale AI systems."
From a market structure perspective, BE Semiconductor holds a critical position in the advanced packaging equipment sector. According to market data, BE Semiconductor accounts for about 70% of the global hybrid bonding equipment market. Its flagship model, the Datacon 8800 CHAMEO ultra plus AC, achieves alignment accuracy of up to 100 nanometers and a throughput of up to 2,000 cycles per hour, with volume production potential.
Demand-side momentum is also strengthening. BE Semiconductor's third-quarter orders surged 96% year over year to €342.6 million (approximately $382.0 million); hybrid bonding equipment orders in the first nine months of 2026 were already more than double the full-year 2025 level. The company's latest financial report shows that its hybrid bonding customer base has expanded to 23 companies, with cumulative equipment demand exceeding 215 units.
It is worth noting that last week the market briefly worried that Dutch semiconductor equipment leader ASML might become a competitor to BE Semiconductor in the hybrid bonding arena, which BE Semiconductor has denied. Against the backdrop of advanced packaging becoming key to the AI chip computing power race, alliances and competitive-cooperative relationships among equipment makers are rapidly intensifying.
On the other hand, Chinese equipment makers are also catching up in hybrid bonding technology. China's Piotech recorded hybrid bonding equipment revenue of CNY 136 million (approximately $20.4 million) in 2025, up 41.92% year over year, and has secured repeat orders for wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding systems, meaning that this niche market previously dominated by a small number of vendors is gradually seeing new suppliers emerge.
For investors, the most direct significance of this deal is that Applied Materials is betting its resources on the "back-end" packaging link of AI chips. As advancing Moore's Law becomes increasingly difficult, improvements in chip performance increasingly depend on advanced packaging and heterogeneous integration, and hybrid bonding is one of the highest-barrier technologies in this area. By tying up with BE Semiconductor through a stake purchase rather than an acquisition, Applied Materials can share technology and customers while avoiding the operational risks and regulatory resistance of full integration.
However, the deal still must pass U.S. antitrust review, and the timetable and conditions remain uncertain. Applied Materials has also stated that it will not pursue board seats or increase its stake further, and whether the cooperation can be translated into substantive orders and revenue contribution will be a key focus for the market going forward.
