Investing.com -- Amkor Technology (NASDAQ:AMKR) shares surged 8% Wednesday following news that Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) plans to significantly expand its advanced packaging partnership with the semiconductor assembly firm into South Korea. 
Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list » 
Under the expanded agreement, Nvidia and Amkor aim to boost advanced packaging capacity in South Korea, targeting a more than 300% increase in interposer wafer capacity by the end of 2028. The initiative, alongside Amkor's ongoing development of new South Korean manufacturing facilities, will support higher production volumes for Nvidia's current and next-generation AI platforms. 
The deal is part of Nvidia's broader effort to scale global manufacturing capacity across multiple supply chain partners to keep pace with surging demand for AI infrastructure. The graphics giant is collaborating with Amkor, IBIDEN, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Siliconware Precision Industries (SPIL), and Unimicron Technology to expand capabilities across substrates, advanced packaging, testing, and optical engines.

Key supply chain developments include: 
Nvidia plans to increase substrate capacity for its products 2.5-fold over the next three years. Samsung Electro-Mechanics joins Nvidia's substrate supply chain immediately via existing South Korean facilities, with production allocated to Nvidia expected to represent a major share of its total package substrate capacity by 2028. Additionally, Nvidia is backing Unimicron's substrate expansion in Taiwan through a capacity reservation agreement, set to bring online capacity starting Q2 2027 and reach full scale by mid-2028. 
Nvidia is providing a $1.1 billion capacity reservation advance to KYEC to fund new U.S. testing facilities and equipment, targeting high-volume production by April 2027. 
SPIL plans to expand Taiwanese manufacturing capacity for optical engines used in co-packaged optics, targeting a 15-fold increase by mid-2027 and double that capacity again by late 2028.

content_text:
Thermo Fisher posts higher third-quarter revenue and earnings as margins improve
Published: 09:04 21 Oct 2026 EDT
Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc (NYSE:TMO, XETRA:TN8) increased third-quarter revenue by 9% to $12.14 billion, while adjusted earnings per share rose 15% to $6.68.
Revenue for the three months ended September 2026 increased from $11.12 billion a year earlier, with organic revenue growth, which excludes the effects of acquisitions, disposals and currency movements, reaching 6%.
Adjusted operating income rose 15% to $2.97 billion, while adjusted operating margin increased to 24.5% from 23.3% in the same period last year.
The company’s generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) diluted earnings per share increased 9% to $4.64, while GAAP operating income rose 17% to $2.26 billion.
GAAP operating margin improved to 18.6% from 17.4%, indicating that the company retained a larger share of revenue as operating profit.
Thermo Fisher chief executive Marc Casper said the company’s growth strategy and its Practical Process Improvement (PPI) Business System supported its performance during the quarter.
The company launched several products during the period, including a mass spectrometer designed for isotope ratio analysis, an electron detector for advanced materials research and a new autoimmune screening test cleared by the US Food and Drug Administration.
Thermo Fisher also partnered with Mayo Clinic to launch Precure, an initiative combining data from more than one million patient samples with its proteomics technologies to support disease research, earlier detection and precision medicine.
In South Korea, the company opened its first artificial intelligence and automation innovation centre to help customers improve research and development productivity.
Thermo Fisher also opened a highly automated distribution centre in Kentucky to improve supply chain speed and flexibility across North America.
The company completed the previously announced sale of its microbiology business during the quarter as part of its capital deployment strategy.
Thermo Fisher said it would provide updated financial guidance for 2026 during its third-quarter earnings conference call.
Shares were down around 2% in early Wednesday morning trading.

content_text:
Wilmington council backs $2 million deal to sweeten odds of landing Corning expansion 
The Wilmington City Council voted unanimously Tuesday night to approve $2 million in incentives for Corning Inc. to expand its operations in the city. 
By Hudson Steiner 
Published : Oct. 20, 2026 at 10:20 PM EDT 
Share 
Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google 
WILMINGTON, N.C. (WECT) - The Wilmington City Council voted unanimously Tuesday night to approve $2 million in incentives for Corning Inc. to expand its operations in the city, following suit with New Hanover County.
The council’s incentive package will provide annual payments of $400,000 a year for five years. In exchange, Corning would invest $585 million and create 414 new jobs.
The vote comes one day after New Hanover County commissioners voted to offer their own incentive package during a meeting Monday, putting up to $600,000 a year for five years from the county’s general fund, which is made up of taxpayer dollars.
PREVIOUS STORY: NHC Commissioners approve incentive for Corning Inc. to expand in Wilmington 
Corning is a glass products manufacturer based in Corning, New York.
“Based in Corning, New York, this multinational technology company specializes in glass, ceramics, and related materials,” Scott Satterfield, CEO of Wilmington Business Development, said during the county’s meeting. “For over 60 years Corning has been a vital employer here.”
Corning officials told commissioners that Wilmington is one of several locations under consideration for the expansion.
If the area is selected, the project would bring new jobs with salaries averaging more than $85,000 a year, along with the $585 million capital investment.
With both the city and county incentives now approved, the combined incentive package totals $5 million. Corning officials are now left to decide whether to proceed with the Wilmington expansion or pursue alternative locations.

content_text:
METiS Enters Collaboration with Eli Lilly for Next-Generation Tissue-Specific LNP Delivery Technologies
Author(s) Nicholas Jacobus 
METiS TechBio enters a collaboration with Eli Lilly to develop next-generation, tissue-specific lipid nanoparticle delivery technologies using METiS’s AI-driven lipid discovery platform.
Advertisement
METiS TechBio announced a strategic collaboration with Eli Lilly and Company focused on researching and discovering novel lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-based delivery solutions designed to enable tissue-specific delivery of therapeutic modalities.
Under the agreement, METiS is eligible to receive an upfront payment in the low double-digit millions of dollars, upwards of approximately $1.1 billion in development, regulatory, and commercial milestone payments, and single-digit tiered royalties on annual net sales of any resulting products. 1 
What will each company contribute?
METiS is expected to apply its proprietary, AI-driven ionizable lipid discovery and optimization platform, AiLNP, to develop next-generation delivery technologies aiming at improving the targeting and biodistribution of LNP-based delivery systems. 1 Eli Lilly is set to contribute its drug discovery, development, and commercialization expertise to advance the collaboration.

Roundup: TRexBio & Retension Pharmaceuticals Announce IPO Pricing 
Roundup: Shionogi Inc. Acquires IntraBio, Gate Bioscience extends Collaboration with Eli Lilly, Alector Enters Global License Agreement with Genentech 
The companies say combining METiS’s generative and predictive AI capabilities for rational LNP design with Eli Lilly’s scientific and development infrastructure is intended to yield novel LNP architectures with improved tissue specificity, enhanced therapeutic performance, and broader applicability across multiple disease areas. 1 
Why does delivery technology matter here?
Lipid nanoparticles have become a central modality for delivering therapeutic payloads to target tissues and cells, underpinning everything from mRNA vaccines to gene-editing therapies. 2 As the industry moves into more complex modalities, the ability to direct payloads precisely to intended tissues, while minimizing off-target exposure, has become a key bottleneck in translating novel therapeutics into approved products. METiS positions AiLNP as an answer to that bottleneck, using generative AI models, including one referred to as PhatGPT, to generate and optimize lipid candidates computationally rather than through traditional trial-and-error screening. 1,2 
What is METiS saying about the deal?
METiS frames the collaboration as validation of its AI-driven approach and an opportunity to scale its platform through a partner with substantial development reach. “Delivery remains a critical determinant of therapeutic success, particularly as the industry expands into increasingly sophisticated modalities,” says Chris Lai, chairman and CEO of METiS TechBio. “We are excited to collaborate with Lilly, a global leader in the discovery and development of innovative medicines. By combining METiS’ AI-powered platform with Lilly’s scientific expertise and development capabilities, we aim to unlock a new generation of tissue-targeted delivery technologies that have the potential to transform how medicines reach patients.”
What’s next? 
Terms of the agreement were not fully disclosed, including which disease areas or specific programs the collaboration will initially target. 1 The deal adds Eli Lilly to a growing list of large pharmaceutical companies turning to AI-native biotechs for delivery innovation, as sponsors look to extend LNP technology beyond its original mRNA vaccine applications into gene therapies, RNA interference, and other emerging modalities.

Arkema Inaugurates New Acrylic Acid Purification Unit 
Arkema has opened a new acrylic acid purification unit at its Carling production site in France, deploying a new process that improves energy efficiency by 25 % and reduces carbon intensity by 20 %. The EUR 150 million investment is part of the company’s broader decarbonisation programme . 
20 October 2026 
Arkema 
Binders 
Expansion 
Save in bookmarks 
Arkema's new acrylic acid purification unit at the Carling site in France marks a significant step in the company's decarbonisation investment programme. 
Source: Arkema 
Advertisement:
Arkema has inaugurated a new acrylic acid purification unit at its Carling site in Saint-Avold, France. The unit operates on a new process and is located at one of Europe’s major acrylic monomer production facilities. Carling produces acrylic monomers used in performance coatings, adhesives, water treatment, and other advanced materials. 
According to Arkema, the new unit improves the energy efficiency of the purification process by 25 % and reduces the carbon intensity of site operations by 20 %. The company also states that the new technology optimises resource and waste management and significantly reduces solvent consumption. Arkema describes the investment as placing the Carling plant among reference sites in the industry, aligned with the highest operational and environmental standards. 
EUR 150 Million Investment Targets Decarbonisation of European Acrylic Production 
The project was decided in 2023 and was partly funded by the French State through the France 2030 programme, operated by ADEME and funded by the European Union via NextGenerationEU. Thierry Le Hénaff, chairman and chief executive officer of Arkema, commented: “With an investment of nearly €150 million, this new unit represents one of Arkema’s largest industrial projects in France. It will contribute to the Group’s ambitious climate plan, underpinned by a dedicated investment program supporting Arkema’s decarbonization, with a cumulative amount that could reach €400 million over the 2022-2030 period.” 
The inauguration ceremony was attended by Le Hénaff and Stéphane Séjourné, executive vice-president of the European Commission for Prosperity and Industrial Strategy. The event was held on the same day as the Critical Chemicals Alliance General Assembly, which brought together European industrial leaders and policymakers to address challenges related to sovereignty, competitiveness, and decarbonisation. 
European Industrial Policy and the Role of Low-Carbon Acrylic Materials 
Séjourné underlined the broader political significance of the investment: “Europe must keep its chemical industry. There can be neither industrial sovereignty nor strategic autonomy if we allow the essential building blocks of our economy to leave. Carling is showing the way forward: nearly EUR 150 million invested to produce in Europe, using less energy and generating less carbon, while building on decades of industrial know-how. This is exactly the model we want to promote: decarbonizing without deindustrializing, investing in our regions, and making our industrial hubs the driving forces of our future.” 
Arkema states that the unit is part of its decarbonisation investment programme and supports what the company describes as its ambitious climate plan. The company adds that the investment strengthens its position in the low-carbon acrylic materials market in Europe.

HyProMag USA deploys third mobile system
Several technology and recycling firms in the United States and Canada have collaborated to invest in mobile systems to process printed circuit boards and hard drives.
“The deployment of our third Inserma system as a mobile processing unit represents an important step in the development of the Dallas-Fort Worth project,” says Julian Treger, CEO of CoTec Holdings.
Photo courtesy of Intelligent Lifecycle Solutions 
By
Brian Taylor, Senior Editor 
Published October 20, 2026
Listen to article 
/ 
A coalition of firms in the United States and Canada, some with ownership stakes in each other, have now deployed three mobile hard disk drive (HDD) separation system designed to recover rare earth element (REE) and magnet materials from discarded electronic components.
Canada-based Mkango Magnetic Materials Ltd. says HyProMag USA LLC, in which it owns a stake, has announced the deployment of its third Spanish-made Inserma Anoia S.L. HDD separation system to be used as a mobile processing unit, “expanding HyProMag USA’s processing and customer engagement capabilities across the U.S.”
Adds Mkango, “The deployment further strengthens HyProMag USA’s partnership with Intelligent Lifecycle Solutions (ILS) and supports the expansion of a scalable nationwide platform for the recovery and recycling of rare earth magnets from end-of-life HDDs.”
ILS is based in Nevada and has processing capacity there and in South Carolina, according to Mkango.
Also involved is HyProMag USA co-owner CoTec Holdings Corp., a Canada-based firm that says it “integrates breakthrough technologies with strategic assets to unlock secure, sustainable, and low-cost supply chains.” 
Mkango says feedstock inventories currently under contract and in storage, together with active procurement programs undertaken by the companies involved, “continue to strengthen the feedstock platform and are expected to support initial commissioning and ramp-up activities” at a planned HyProMag USA Texas Hub facility in the Dallas-Fort Worth scheduled to open in 2028.
The Canadian company says Delaware-based HyProMag USA also has completed commercial sales of recovered printed circuit board (PCB) material to downstream smelter partners, generating revenue that supports the acquisition and retention of magnet-bearing feedstock inventory.
“The deployment of our third Inserma system as a mobile processing unit represents an important step in the development of the Dallas-Fort Worth project,” says Julian Treger, CEO of CoTec Holdings.
“Together with continued progress in feedstock sourcing and commercial PCB recovery, it strengthens our operating platform and expands our ability to engage directly with customers across multiple end markets,” adds Treger.
Remars Graham Davy, Managing Director of ILS , “The focus of the ILS team has been on demonstrating that HDDs can be efficiently processed into separate, marketable material streams. The mobile unit allows us to work directly with customers at their facilities, supporting trial programs, demonstrating material recovery performance and creating opportunities to secure additional feedstock supply.”
The companies say they are tapping into diversified feedstock channels “across industrial, health care, government and IT asset disposition sectors.”

20th October 2026
Submitted by:
Andrew Warmington
Sumitomo Chemical has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with India’s Tata Electronics to explore a possible collaboration in semiconductor fabrication. The company will examine specific measures aimed at establishing a stable supply system for materials, possibly including a semiconductor chemicals facility in India.
Sumitomo Chemical’s ICT & Mobility Solutions sector is one of its growth drivers and the semiconductor materials business has been designated as a priority area within it. The business offers advanced photoresists and semiconductor chemicals, being particularly known for high-purity chemicals.
In recent years, Sumitomo Chemical has expanded its semiconductor chemicals capacity in Japan and South Korea, while establishing a new base in Texas. Earlier this year, it acquired Asia Union Electronic Chemical, with facilities in Taiwan and Nevada. It has also begun operations at advanced high-purity chemical centres in Japan and South Korea to develop new processes and recycling technologies.
Another Japanese player, Nissan Chemical, has separately established a wholly-owned subsidiary in Zhangjiagang in China’s Jiangsu province. This will make anti-reflective coatings for the photoresists and multilayer materials used in semiconductors. The company said that demand for semiconductors in China has continued to expand, driven by ongoing digitalisation and other factors, whilecustomer demand for supply chain resilience has grown.

Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany to Acquire Silence Therapeutics, Strengthening Rare Disease Pipeline with Innovative siRNA Asset 
We enter into a definitive agreement to acquire biotechnology company Silence Therapeutics, focused on siRNA-therapies in areas of high unmet need. 
Subscribe
Share 
Icons revealed to the left 
19 Oct 2026 
| 
Darmstadt, Germany 
Purchase price of $20 per ADS in cash represents an enterprise value of $1.1 billion and an equity value of approximately $1.3 billion 
Silence Therapeutics is a UK-headquartered biotechnology company with a potentially best-in-class Phase 3-ready investigational siRNA therapy for rare disease, polycythemia vera (PV) 
Planned acquisition will strengthen the position of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany in rare diseases, a high-value growth driver, and advance its Healthcare ambition to become a leading Global Specialty Innovator 
Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, a leading science and technology company, today announced its entry into a definitive agreement to acquire Silence Therapeutics plc (Nasdaq: SLN), a global clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in London, UK, focused on pioneering the design and development of siRNA (short interfering RNA) therapies in areas of high unmet need.
The purchase price of $20 per ADS in cash, with each ADS representing three ordinary shares of Silence Therapeutics (or $6.6667 per ordinary share), represents an enterprise value of $1.1 billion and an equity value of approximately $1.3 billion. The consideration represents an 82% premium to Silence Therapeutics’ 30-day volume-weighted average price of $10.99, as of the close of trading on October 16, 2026, the last trading day prior to the transaction announcement. The transaction is subject to satisfaction of customary closing conditions.
“The planned acquisition of Silence Therapeutics will strengthen our capabilities to serve patients with targeted specialty and rare diseases,” said Kai Beckmann, Chairman of the Executive Board and Group CEO of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany. “Following the acquisition of SpringWorks Therapeutics last year, we continue to transform our pipeline toward areas of high specialization and unmet medical need, with an ongoing commitment to external innovation. The proposed transaction follows our strategic priority to address attractive end markets also through M&A, creating value over the mid- to long-term.”
The transaction, once completed, will add Divesiran ─ a potentially best-in-class, phase 3-ready siRNA investigational therapy, in development for phlebotomy-dependent polycythemia vera (PV) ─ to Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany’s pipeline. Divesiran is dosed subcutaneously once every 3 months.
PV is a chronic myeloproliferative neoplasm ─ a type of rare blood cancer ─ characterized by the excessive production of red blood cells, which can be associated with a higher rate of death from cardiovascular and thrombotic events.
Divesiran is designed to selectively silence TMPRSS6, a gene involved in regulating hepcidin, the body’s key regulator of iron metabolism. By increasing hepcidin levels, Divesiran aims to limit iron availability for red blood cell production, helping to control hematocrit levels and potentially reducing the need for frequent therapeutic phlebotomies.
Divesiran met its primary endpoint in the Phase 2 SANRECO study with an 88% responder rate versus 19% for placebo (p “The planned acquisition of Silence Therapeutics marks a significant step forward in our strategy to become a Global Specialty Innovator in Healthcare,” said Danny Bar-Zohar, member of the Executive Board and CEO Healthcare at Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany. “Silence Therapeutics’ primary siRNA pipeline asset, Divesiran, is supported by promising Phase 2 efficacy data, a potentially best-in-class, once-every-three-month dosing schedule, and a safety profile that appears manageable, with the added advantage of targeting a well-defined, homogeneous patient population. The planned acquisition also provides an entry point into hematology through a biologically validated mechanism of action. With this transaction, we are advancing our efforts to build a differentiated, sustainable pipeline as we bring more medicines to more patients, faster.”
“We are pleased to have reached this agreement with Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, which follows a competitive sale process and delivers significant, immediate and certain value to our shareholders,” said Iain Ross, Interim Principal Executive Officer and Chairman of the Silence Therapeutics’ Board. “This transaction follows potentially best-in-class Phase 2 polycythemia vera data for Divesiran and reflects the important progress we have made advancing our differentiated siRNA pipeline. It also provides a new home for our innovative programs within Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, placing Divesiran with a company that has the scale, resources and commercial capabilities to accelerate its Phase 3 development and bring this potentially best-in-class siRNA therapy to patients in need. We are incredibly grateful to our employees for their dedication and contributions in building Silence Therapeutics into the company it is today.”
The transaction has been unanimously approved by Silence Therapeutics’ Board of Directors and Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany’s relevant corporate bodies and is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to satisfaction of customary closing conditions, including receipt of required regulatory approvals and approval by Silence Therapeutics’ shareholders. In connection with the transaction, certain securityholders of Silence Therapeutics holding securities representing approximately 14% of Silence Therapeutics’ voting power have entered into a voting and support agreement with Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, under which the securityholders have agreed among other things, to vote their voting securities of Silence Therapeutics in favor of the transaction. Silence Therapeutics is a UK company, with ADSs, each representing three of its ordinary shares, listed on NASDAQ. As is customary for similar transactions, the transaction will be effected through a UK scheme of arrangement.
The planned acquisition will be funded through proceeds from new debt.
Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany is committed to leveraging advanced technologies and data science to accelerate the discovery and delivery of breakthrough medicines. This acquisition is another step forward in its broader strategy to enhance research productivity and the output of its pipeline sustainably, focusing on indications that can be derisked through proper preclinical and early clinical testing to ensure that more patients gain access to effective treatments.
Silence Therapeutics employs approximately 80 people and operates from locations in the UK, the US and Germany.
A&O Shearman is acting as legal counsel to Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany.

The week in cell therapy 
This week: a new manufacturing facility for Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) grade small molecules opened in Bristol, UK, a collaboration leveraging cGMP Next-Generation Sequencing-based viral safety testing to advance a stem cell therapy for osteoarthritis was announced, and a pre-clinical CAR-T portfolio was sold for €8 million.
The news highlights:
New UK facility boosts GMP small molecule manufacturing for cell therapies 
Collaboration to advance stem cell therapy for osteoarthritis 
Early-stage CAR-T portfolio sold for €8 million 
New UK facility boosts GMP small molecule manufacturing for cell therapies
Bio-Techne Corporation (MN, USA) has announced the opening of its new purpose-built 10,000-square-foot GMP manufacturing facility in Bristol, UK, strengthening the company’s global GMP manufacturing infrastructure.
The facility has five ISO-8 multifunctional cleanrooms and two ISO-7 cleanrooms dedicated to small molecule manufacturing and product handling.
“As the cell therapy field continues to mature, success increasingly depends on the ability to manufacture therapies consistently and at scale,” said Kim Kelderman, President and Chief Executive Officer of Bio-Techne. “Our investment in Bristol demonstrates Bio-Techne’s commitment to providing customers with the GMP materials, manufacturing expertise, and supply chain reliability needed to accelerate development and ultimately bring transformative therapies to patients worldwide.”
Read more 
Collaboration to advance stem cell therapy for osteoarthritis
Charles River Laboratories (MA, USA) and Magellan Stem Cells (Victoria, Australia) have announced a partnership to advance the development and commercialization of Magellan’s lead proprietary allogeneic, off-the-shelf stem cell therapy candidate (Zelestrocel) for osteoarthritis.
Magellan has recently completed Phase I/II trials for Zelestrocel and is now moving toward a Phase III study. The company has also built manufacturing capacity directly into its development process, having obtained GMP certification from Australia’s Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) for its production site in Melbourne.
Under the agreement, Charles River will provide cGMP Next-Generation Sequencing-based viral safety testing for Zelestrocel to support regulatory readiness.
“As we prepare for the next stage of Zelestrocel’s development, having access to advanced testing technologies and collaborating with experienced partners is critical to our success,” said Magellan Stem Cells CEO Julien Freitag.
Read more 
Early-stage CAR-T portfolio sold for €8 million
Lakefront Biotherapeutics (formerly Galapagos NV; Mechelen, Belgium) has announced the completed sale of its early-stage cell therapy portfolio to Armed Cell Therapeutics (Brussels, Belgium). Under the deal terms, Lakefront will receive €8 million upfront, with the possibility of earning up to $230 million in future milestone payments plus a modest royalty on sales.
The divested assets include a range of multi-targeting and armed CAR-T constructs engineered to enhance the potency and persistence of CAR-T therapies while addressing treatment resistance in hematological cancers and solid tumors.
“I’m pleased we were able to complete this sale of the early-stage cell therapy programs as it provides a path to continue to advance these assets on behalf of patients. Additionally, it offers Lakefront shareholders the opportunity to benefit from their potential future progress by the experienced team at Armed Cell Therapeutics,” said Sooin Kwon, Chief Business Officer of Lakefront. “Lakefront continues to be in an enviable position with a rich legacy of innovation, an exciting newly established pipeline of T-cell engagers and a strong cash balance.”

Air Products and Chemicals (APD) has signed a definitive agreement to design, build and run an LNG based air separation unit at the Pengerang LNG regasification terminal in Johor, targeting an early 2027 start up. 
Recent price action suggests investors are warming to Air Products and Chemicals again. A 1-day share price return of 1.79% and a 7-day share price return of 2.83% have lifted the stock to US$288.96, even though the 90-day share price return is down 1.61% and the 1-year total shareholder return is 13.22%. 
Scan beyond Air Products and Chemicals and review hand picked industrial gas peers and infrastructure players screened as list of solid balance sheet and fundamentals (25 results) 
So is this latest upswing in Air Products and Chemicals a vote of confidence in its industrial gas projects and earnings profile, or just sentiment snapping back after a softer patch? And what does that imply for valuation next? 
Most Popular Narrative: 16% Undervalued 
On the most followed narrative, Air Products and Chemicals screens as undervalued, with a fair value estimate of $345.11 versus the latest close at $288.96. That gap rests heavily on how its project pipeline and capital discipline play out. 
Capital discipline and portfolio optimization, including the decision not to proceed with the Louisiana Clean Energy Complex and several other clean energy projects and the related plan to lower annual capex toward about US$2.0b to US$2.5b with roughly US$1.5b focused on traditional industrial gas projects, may free cash for higher return uses and support future return on capital and free cash flow. 
Expansion in growth end markets such as electronics, including about US$3b of traditional industrial gas backlog with more than US$1.5b of recent project wins, multiple long term semiconductor gas contracts in Korea, Taiwan, and Arizona, and long term helium agreements expected to more than double helium volumes to large Asian electronics customers between 2026 and 2030, positions Air Products and Chemicals for additional volume based revenue and asset driven earnings once these projects come onstream.

Still, Air Products and Chemicals faces two clear swing factors: any renewed capex creep on mega projects and helium pricing or supply setbacks in electronics.

Another View: What Multiples Say About Air Products and Chemicals

ASML Earnings: Capacity Plan Falls Short of Demand; 2029-30 Order Visibility Is the Next Catalyst 
Upgrades were the main driver of the 57.5% gross margin this quarter.
Javier Correonero Oct 14, 2026 
Share 
Sander Hofman/ASML Securities in This Article
ASML Holding NV ADR
(ASML)
Key Morningstar Metrics for ASML Holding 
Fair Value Estimate : $2,050.00
Morningstar Rating : ★★★
Morningstar Economic Moat Rating : Wide
Morningstar Uncertainty Rating : High
What We Thought of ASML Holding’s Earnings 
Last quarter, ASML Holding ASML announced plans to expand low-NA EUV and immersion DUV capacity by 30% in 2027 and another 30% in 2028. These plans seem already outdated, as management has acknowledged this might not be enough to meet customer demand.
Why it matters: ASML’s backlog keeps growing, with 2027 fully booked and significant order intake already for 2028. In our view, the most important disclosure from these earnings was that ASML is having first conversations with customers for 2029 and 2030 orders. DRAM makers seem the most open to talking about 2029-30 already.
While we still see some upside to our 2028 revenue and EPS forecast as ASML tries to expand capacity beyond 30% with its existing footprint, we believe most of it is already priced in. What could push the stock higher is order visibility that confirms 2029 and 2030 as “growth years.”
The bottom line: We maintain our wide Morningstar Economic Moat Rating and EUR 1,800 fair value estimate.
After 28% sales growth in both 2027 and 2028, reaching EUR 56 and EUR 71.5 billion respectively, we model a return to low-double-digit growth in 2029 and 2030, with sales reaching EUR 88 billion in 2030. Should management confirm the first 2029 orders over the next six months, our 2029-30 forecast would gain credibility, and the stock price could converge toward our fair value estimate.
Our bull case would require 2029 to book as quickly and as fully as 2028 has. If customers place orders at a fast pace in the coming months, sales growth in 2029-30 could exceed our low-double-digit forecast.
Key stats: Beyond expanding capacity, ASML continues to aggressively develop upgrades to low-NA EUV and immersion DUV output. Installed base management revenue reached EUR 3.3 billion, EUR 400 million higher than expected, thanks to the upgrade business, as customers look to extract more productivity from their machines. Upgrades were the main driver of the 57.5% gross margin this quarter, above guidance of 55.0%-57.0%.

ASML says it's getting order interest through 2030 as profit smashes expectations
Published Wed, Oct 14 2026 1:14 AM EDT Updated Wed, Oct 14 2026 4:45 AM EDT 
Arjun Kharpal @/in/arjunkharpal/ @ArjunKharpal 
WATCH LIVE 
Key Points
ASML said some customers are "expressing an interest" in placing orders with the company in 2029 and 2030, providing investors with a view into longer-term demand.
The Dutch chip giant said it is looking at ways to increase capacity for 2028 beyond the 30% increase it had previously forecast as demand remains strong.
The company also raised the lower end of its sales forecast for 2026.
In this article
ASML 
TSM 
Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT 
ASML said Wednesday that some of its customers are expressing interest in placing orders for its critical semiconductor tools for 2029 and 2030 as the company reported third-quarter profit that beat expectations.
The comments will likely comfort investors who have been looking to assess the longer-term demand outlook for ASML's lithography machines.
"Our customers continue to increase their short- and medium-term equipment demand forecasts with us, driven primarily by their views on the size and duration of AI-related investments," CEO Christophe Fouquet said in a press release. 
"In light of their demand visibility, some customers are expressing an interest in placing orders with us for 2029 and even 2030."
ASML is the only company in the world that produces extreme ultraviolet lithography machines, a key tool used by the likes of TSMC to make the world's most advanced semiconductors. 
Investors closely watch the Dutch company's earnings for signs of AI-related chip demand. 
watch now 
VIDEO 3:47 03:47 
ASML races to expand capacity on strong AI-driven demand
Squawk Box Europe 
Fouquet said current supply planned for 2027 and 2028 will not fully meet the demand of its customers. The company is "investigating ways" to increase capacity for 2028 beyond the 30% increase it had previously forecast. 
ASML has now updated its guidance three times this year, upping its full-year forecast for the second time in July, and on Wednesday it raised the lower end of its sales forecast for 2026. 
The company now expects net sales of between 44 billion euros and 45 billion euros ($49.3 billion to $50.4 billion). The previous lower end of the forecast was for 43 billion euros.
ASML also said it expects fourth-quarter net sales of between 14.2 billion euros and 15.2 billion euros. The upper end of the range is ahead of LSEG consensus estimates of 14.2 billion euros. 
ASML's stock was around 2% higher in early trade in Europe. Shares of the company have rallied 56% this year. 
ASML shares year-to-date
During the quarter, Samsung and TSMC, the world's two biggest chipmakers, committed to using ASML's High NA extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines. High NA EUV is ASML's next-generation tool, which analysts see as key to the Dutch firm's future growth.
For the third quarter, here's how ASML did versus LSEG consensus estimates:
Net sales: 11.66 billion euros versus 11.72 billion euros expected
Net profit: 4.96 billion euros versus 4.1 billion euros expected 
ASML sticks to China forecast 
The semiconductor equipment maker said it expects China sales to account for 20% of its total business, sticking to a prior forecast.
While ASML holds an effective monopoly on EUV machines, a July report from The Information suggested an unnamed Chinese company had begun manufacturing an immersion deep ultraviolet lithography (DUV) machine, citing people familiar with the matter.
ASML dominates the manufacturing of DUV machines, which are less advanced than EUV. China has been ramping up its domestic semiconductor supply chain, with some investors concerned it could challenge the European and U.S. dominance. However, analysts raised questions about China's ability to ramp up its own DUV technology. 
ASML meanwhile has faced challenges in China over the last few years. The company is restricted from selling EUV and some DUV tools to China.

Rio Tinto expects lithium output to be constrained by weather and delays in Argentina, while still waiting on Chile 
Bnamericas Published: Wednesday, October 14, 2026 
Production Public-private partnership (PPP) Market Prices and Forecasts Lithium Electrolyte Building Materials Brine extraction Evaporation Mergers & Acquisitions Environmental conflict Private Investment Lithium Financing Project Finance Lithium Hydroxide Prospecting, exploration and extraction of mineral resources Direct lithium extraction (DLE) Mining Companies Lithium Carbonate Show 13 More Hide 13 Topics 
Rio Tinto increased lithium output in 3Q26 and pressed on with construction of its Rincon project and commissioning of the Fénix 1B expansion in Argentina, though logistics problems at Sal de Vida and poor weather will weigh on its full-year performance.
For 2026, the Anglo-Australian miner expects to come in at the low end of its 61,000-64,000t global lithium production guidance, hit by maintenance at its assets and delays in the ramp-up of Sal de Vida due to equipment availability.
Sal de Vida, built with initial capacity of 15,000t/y of lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE), achieved first production in 2Q26.
At Salar de Olaroz, in which Rio holds a 66.5% stake, output was affected by scheduled annual maintenance and lower lithium concentrations in the evaporation ponds as a result of adverse weather linked to the El Niño phenomenon.
At Fénix, the 1B expansion, which adds 10,000t/y of LCE and secures a 40-year life for the operation, is progressing well, although scheduled annual maintenance on lines 0 and 1A hit 3Q26 output. Fénix mainly uses direct lithium extraction (DLE) technology.
At Rincon, a US$2.5bn project, construction is ongoing. Earthworks and infrastructure works were carried out in 3Q26, and the camp expansion moved forward.
Rincon is slated to start production in 2028, followed by a three-year ramp-up to full capacity of 60,000t/y of battery-grade LCE over a 40-year life using selective adsorption DLE technology.
Two hubs 
Rio Tinto plans two lithium hubs in Argentina. One will be in Catamarca province, home to Fénix and Sal de Vida in the Salar del Hombre Muerto, which holds some 19Mt of LCE.
The second will span Salta and Jujuy provinces and comprise Rincon, Olaroz and Cauchari, around the Olaroz, Cauchari and Rincón salt flats, which together hold 37Mt of LCE.
Chile 
In Chile, Rio Tinto expects to finalize its binding agreements with state-owned companies between late 2026 and early 2027.
With Codelco, it will develop the Salar de Maricunga project through a joint venture in which Rio will hold a 49.9% stake, while with Enami it will develop Salares Altoandinos through another JV in which it will hold 51%.
Both projects are located in the Atacama region in northern Chile, and although they have high potential in terms of resource quality, development has been slower than expected.
Unlike in Argentina, lithium in Chile is not subject to mining concessions, so only the state or its companies can exploit it, along with private firms that obtain special contracts from the mining ministry.
"The non-concessibility of Chilean lithium is a barrier to production. The right approach would be to allow concessions to private companies under appropriate regulation," Santiago Montt, CEO of law firm Montt Group, told BNamericas.
Montt believes Chile's current lithium system neither protects the interests of indigenous peoples nor generates more jobs or wealth for the country.
Finance and market 
The results come amid a favorable lithium market. In 3Q26, LCE prices averaged US$19,000/t, supported by strong and growing demand from battery energy storage systems (BESS), according to Rio Tinto's latest report.
Rio has managed its capital efficiently and closed 3Q26 with agreements that have already allowed it to reallocate more than US$2bn to higher-return opportunities, including lithium sales contracts with prepayments.

VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / October 13, 2026 / CoTec Holdings Corp. (TSXV:CTH)(OTCQX:CTHCF) (“CoTec” or the “Company”) notes the press release issued today by its joint venture, HyProMag USA, LLC (“HyProMag USA”), providing an update on development activities for its Texas Hub rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing project in Dallas-Fort Worth, Texas (the “Texas Hub”). Following the commencement of formal power supply discussions announced on June 22, 2026, i HyProMag USA has secured electrical power capacity with Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC (“Oncor”) for the Texas Hub development and expects the facility’s electricity requirements to be supplied predominantly from renewable energy resources.
Key Highlights 
Power capacity secured: Power capacity secured with Oncor for both cutting and finishing operations and the Phase 1 development, with a pathway through a sub-station upgrade to provide power for Phase 2.
Contractor selection and permitting underway: Pegasus TSI, Inc. (“Pegasus”) has commenced contractor selection for cutting and finishing operations and Weston Solutions, Inc. (“Weston”) is advancing permitting activities.
Cutting and finishing operations targeted for H1 2027: Targeted commissioning of cutting and finishing operations in H1 2027 with the processing of neodymium iron boron (“NdFeB”) magnet blocks, initially supplied from HyProMag Group operations, to produce finished magnets.
Phase 1 development: Phase 1 development is targeted for completion in mid-2028 and is designed to produce approximately 550 tonnes per annum (“tpa”) of NdFeB magnet blocks and finished magnets and approximately 484 tpa of co-products, representing approximately 1,034 tpa of total payable production.
Phase 2 development: Phase 2 development envisions expansion to approximately 1,526 tpa of total payable production.
Renewable energy supply: Electricity supply expected to be sourced predominantly from renewable energy resources.
Julian Treger, Chief Executive Officer of CoTec Holdings Corp., commented: “Securing power with Oncor, advancing permitting activities through Weston Solutions and commencing contractor selection are important milestones for the Texas Hub. Initial cutting and finishing operations in 2027 are expected to establish U.S. magnet finishing and qualification capabilities aligned with internationally recognized magnetic material and quality standards, while the full Phase 1 development will deliver integrated recycling and magnet manufacturing capacity. Together, these activities further de-risk the project and demonstrate continued progress towards establishing a domestic and sustainable rare earth magnet supply chain in the United States.” 
Cutting and Finishing Operations 
Cutting and finishing operations in 2027 comprise the initial magnet finishing and qualification facility, enabling production and qualification of finished NdFeB magnets using magnet blocks supplied from HyProMag Group operations. The facility is designed to process NdFeB magnet blocks and support qualification of finished magnets in accordance with ASTM A977/A977M, the national classification standard for magnetic materials, together with quality management systems aligned with ISO 9001 and customer-specific quality, performance and traceability requirements. The objective is to establish qualification capabilities that meet the requirements of U.S. customers and establish a strategic training facility for the finishing of NdFeB magnets in advance of the main Texas Hub developments.
Permitting and Contractor Selection 
Weston is advancing permitting activities for the Texas Hub, while HyProMag USA’s engineering partner Pegasus has commenced a Request for Quotation (“RFQ”) process for the selection of a general contractor for cutting and finishing operations. Pegasus and BBA USA Inc. are HyProMag USA’s U.S.-based engineering, procurement and construction management firms.
Phase 1 and Phase 2 Development 
Phase 1 represents the first integrated recycling and magnet manufacturing stage of the Texas Hub and is designed to produce approximately 550 tpa of sintered NdFeB magnet blocks and finished magnets, together with approximately 484 tpa of co-products, representing total payable production of approximately 1,034 tpa. Upon completion of Phase 2, the Texas Hub is expected to produce approximately 1,048 tpa of sintered NdFeB magnet blocks and cylinders, together with approximately 478 tpa of co-products, representing total payable production of approximately 1,526 tpa.
About HyProMag USA 
HyProMag USA is developing advanced rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing operations to establish a secure domestic U.S. supply chain for NdFeB magnets, essential components for AI infrastructure, defense systems, robotics, electric vehicles, and advanced electronics. Leveraging the revolutionary Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap (“HPMS”) technology, developed over 15 years with over US$100 million in R&D investment, HyProMag USA delivers faster magnet-to-magnet short-loop recycling that uses 88% less energy and reduces carbon emissions by 85% compared to conventional methods. HPMS accepts a wide range of magnet-bearing feedstocks – including end-of-life EV motors, data-center and industrial equipment, consumer electronics, and manufacturing scrap – enabling recovery of magnet-grade material without chemical processing.
Ownership 
HyProMag USA LLC is owned 50:50 by CoTec and HyProMag Limited. HyProMag Limited is 100% owned by Maginito Limited, which is owned 79.4% by Mkango Magnetic Materials Limited (AIM/TSX-V: MKA) and 20.6% by CoTec.
For more information on HyProMag USA, please visit www.hypromagusa.com

CoTec Holdings Corp. (TSXV:CTH)(OTCQX:CTHCF) is redefining the future of resource extraction and recycling. Focused on rare earth magnets and strategic materials, CoTec integrates breakthrough technologies with strategic assets to unlock secure, sustainable, and low-cost supply chains.

By investing in and deploying disruptive technologies, the Company delivers capital-efficient, scalable solutions that transform marginal assets, tailings, waste streams, and recycled products into high-value critical minerals.

CoTec Holdings Corp. Notes HyproMag USA Secures Power and Advances Project Readiness for Texas Rare Earth Magnet Recycling and Manufacturing Hub
Investing News Network 
October 13, 2026 
VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / October 13, 2026 / CoTec Holdings Corp. ( TSXV:CTH )(OTCQX:CTHCF) ("CoTec" or the "Company") notes the press release issued today by its joint venture, HyProMag USA, LLC ("HyProMag USA"), providing an update on development activities for its Texas Hub rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing project in Dallas-Fort Worth, Texas (the "Texas Hub"). Following the commencement of formal power supply discussions announced on June 22, 2026, i HyProMag USA has secured electrical power capacity with Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC ("Oncor") for the Texas Hub development and expects the facility's electricity requirements to be supplied predominantly from renewable energy resources.
Key Highlights 
Power capacity secured: Power capacity secured with Oncor for both cutting and finishing operations and the Phase 1 development, with a pathway through a sub-station upgrade to provide power for Phase 2.
Contractor selection and permitting underway: Pegasus TSI, Inc. ("Pegasus") has commenced contractor selection for cutting and finishing operations and Weston Solutions, Inc. ("Weston") is advancing permitting activities.
Cutting and finishing operations targeted for H1 2027: Targeted commissioning of cutting and finishing operations in H1 2027 with the processing of neodymium iron boron ("NdFeB") magnet blocks, initially supplied from HyProMag Group operations, to produce finished magnets.
Phase 1 development: Phase 1 development is targeted for completion in mid-2028 and is designed to produce approximately 550 tonnes per annum ("tpa") of NdFeB magnet blocks and finished magnets and approximately 484 tpa of co-products, representing approximately 1,034 tpa of total payable production.
Phase 2 development: Phase 2 development envisions expansion to approximately 1,526 tpa of total payable production.
Renewable energy supply: Electricity supply expected to be sourced predominantly from renewable energy resources.
Julian Treger, Chief Executive Officer of CoTec Holdings Corp. , commented: "Securing power with Oncor, advancing permitting activities through Weston Solutions and commencing contractor selection are important milestones for the Texas Hub. Initial cutting and finishing operations in 2027 are expected to establish U.S. magnet finishing and qualification capabilities aligned with internationally recognized magnetic material and quality standards, while the full Phase 1 development will deliver integrated recycling and magnet manufacturing capacity. Together, these activities further de-risk the project and demonstrate continued progress towards establishing a domestic and sustainable rare earth magnet supply chain in the United States." 
Cutting and Finishing Operations 
Cutting and finishing operations in 2027 comprise the initial magnet finishing and qualification facility, enabling production and qualification of finished NdFeB magnets using magnet blocks supplied from HyProMag Group operations. The facility is designed to process NdFeB magnet blocks and support qualification of finished magnets in accordance with ASTM A977/A977M, the national classification standard for magnetic materials, together with quality management systems aligned with ISO 9001 and customer-specific quality, performance and traceability requirements. The objective is to establish qualification capabilities that meet the requirements of U.S. customers and establish a strategic training facility for the finishing of NdFeB magnets in advance of the main Texas Hub developments.
Permitting and Contractor Selection 
Weston is advancing permitting activities for the Texas Hub, while HyProMag USA's engineering partner Pegasus has commenced a Request for Quotation ("RFQ") process for the selection of a general contractor for cutting and finishing operations. Pegasus and BBA USA Inc. are HyProMag USA's U.S.-based engineering, procurement and construction management firms.
Phase 1 and Phase 2 Development 
Phase 1 represents the first integrated recycling and magnet manufacturing stage of the Texas Hub and is designed to produce approximately 550 tpa of sintered NdFeB magnet blocks and finished magnets, together with approximately 484 tpa of co-products, representing total payable production of approximately 1,034 tpa. Upon completion of Phase 2, the Texas Hub is expected to produce approximately 1,048 tpa of sintered NdFeB magnet blocks and cylinders, together with approximately 478 tpa of co-products, representing total payable production of approximately 1,526 tpa.
About HyProMag USA 
HyProMag USA is developing advanced rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing operations to establish a secure domestic U.S. supply chain for NdFeB magnets, essential components for AI infrastructure, defense systems, robotics, electric vehicles, and advanced electronics. Leveraging the revolutionary Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap ("HPMS") technology, developed over 15 years with over US$100 million in R&D investment, HyProMag USA delivers faster magnet-to-magnet short-loop recycling that uses 88% less energy and reduces carbon emissions by 85% compared to conventional methods. HPMS accepts a wide range of magnet-bearing feedstocks - including end-of-life EV motors, data-center and industrial equipment, consumer electronics, and manufacturing scrap - enabling recovery of magnet-grade material without chemical processing.
Ownership 
HyProMag USA LLC is owned 50:50 by CoTec and HyProMag Limited. HyProMag Limited is 100% owned by Maginito Limited, which is owned 79.4% by Mkango Magnetic Materials Limited (AIM/TSX-V: MKA) and 20.6% by CoTec.
For more information on HyProMag USA, please visit www.hypromagusa.com 
About CoTec 
CoTec Holdings Corp. ( TSXV:CTH )(OTCQX:CTHCF) is redefining the future of resource extraction and recycling. Focused on rare earth magnets and strategic materials, CoTec integrates breakthrough technologies with strategic assets to unlock secure, sustainable, and low-cost supply chains.
CoTec's mission is clear: accelerate the energy transition while strengthening strategic mineral supply chains for the countries we operate in. By investing in and deploying disruptive technologies, the Company delivers capital-efficient, scalable solutions that transform marginal assets, tailings, waste streams, and recycled products into high-value critical minerals.
From its HyProMag USA magnet recycling joint venture in Texas, to iron tailings reprocessing and reclamation in Québec, to next-generation copper and iron solutions backed by global majors, CoTec is building a diversified portfolio with long-term growth, rapid cash flow potential, and high barriers to entry. The result is a differentiated platform at the intersection of technology, sustainability, and strategic materials.
For more information, please visit www.cotec.ca

​Overview
CoTec Holdings (TSXV:CTH, OTCQX:CTHCF) is redefining the future of rare earth magnet recycling and strategic material extraction. Its portfolio spans rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing, iron tailings reprocessing and emerging copper extraction technologies, all directed at fast-tracking revenue generation and reducing energy and capital intensity compared to conventional mining.
Key Technologies
The company’s modular, capital-efficient model — including joint ventures and strategic subsidiaries — positions it for scalable growth and streamlined execution. With significant advancement in project execution, one completed feasibility study and a second underway, CoTec is moving toward transforming its technology suite into commercial operations.
Why Invest in CoTec?
Differentiated Growth Model: Capital-light strategy deploying modular technologies at brownfield assets to accelerate timelines and reduce capital intensity.
Strategic Commodity Exposure: Exposure to rare earths, iron and copper — key materials for electrification, AI infrastructure, robotics and other critical supply chains.
Execution-Stage Portfolio: Three projects advancing through feasibility, engineering and financing stages.
Aligned Leadership: Strong insider ownership and experienced management with deep mining and capital markets expertise.
Lower-Carbon Production: Technologies designed to reduce energy use, water consumption and emissions relative to conventional mining.
Investor Insight
CoTec Holdings combines proprietary processing technologies with undervalued and legacy resource assets to create high-margin opportunities across rare earths , iron and copper sectors. With three execution-stage projects and a significant discount to attributable NAV, CoTec provides differentiated exposure to strategic minerals tied to electrification, AI infrastructure and supply-chain security.
Company Highlights
Technology-Driven Value Creatio n: Deploys proprietary, low-carbon processing technologies to extract value from waste, tailings and marginal deposits that traditional mining overlooks.
Execution-Stage Projects : Advancing three core assets — HyProMag USA rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing, the Lac Jeannine iron tailings project, and MagIron iron ore feedstock, concentrator and pelletizer — with clear development pathways.
Expanding Rare Earth Footprint: HyProMag USA advances its scalable US hub-and-spoke rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing roll-out using the Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap (“HPMS”) technology, with Inserma HDD pre-processing machines on site in South Carolina and Nevada, supporting feedstock preparation and future commissioning.
Strategic Copper Focus : Established a new subsidiary, CoTec Copper , to accelerate targeted investment in copper tailings and copper sulfide deposits globally, leveraging CoTec’s core technologies to unlock value.
Iron Ore & Green Steel : Advancing iron tailings reprocessing at Lac Jeannine and supporting the restart of the MagIron pellet project to supply high-grade feedstock for low-carbon steel production.
Strong Insider Support : Management and insiders own a majority of shares, reinforcing alignment with long-term value creation.
Experienced Leadership : Board and executives bring deep mining, technology and capital markets experience from leading global organizations.
Key Technologies and Assets
HyProMag USA Project
HyProMag USA is CoTec’s flagship rare earth recycling platform and a cornerstone of its strategy to localize critical mineral supply chains. The project deploys Hydrogen Processing of Magnetic Scrap technology to recover neodymium iron boron magnets from end-of-life electronics and industrial equipment through a simplified hydrogen-based process that bypasses traditional chemical separation and smelting. This short-loop approach dramatically reduces energy use, water consumption and emissions while lowering operating complexity and cost.
The company’s phased development plan is targeting commissioning of its initial finished neodymium-iron-boron magnet production equipment in Texas in 2027. Up to 20 tonnes of magnet blocks supplied by HyProMag Group in the United Kingdom and Germany will be shaped and finished at HyProMag USA's operations for U.S. customers. Integrated Texas Hub's Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap section targeted for Q2 2028.
Watch an overview of HyProMag USA here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v0d7rKdwu_s 
Highlights 
CoTec holds a 60.3 percent economic interest.
Bankable Feasibility Study supports a single hub after-tax NPV of US$797 million at forecast prices or US$416 million at current prices with recent updated economics published June 22, 2026
Capex estimated at US$152 million per hub.
First revenue targeted for Q2 2028.
Expansion concept envisions three hubs producing 4,656 tonnes annually with potential NPV of up to US$2.2 billion.
Inserma pre-processing machines have arrived at South Carolina and Nevada facilities to support feedstock preparation and scale-up of the hub-and-spoke rollout.
Integrated Texas Hub's Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap section targeted for Q2 2028.
Lac Jeannine Iron Project
The Lac Jeannine project is an advanced tailings reprocessing initiative designed to transform legacy mining waste into high-purity iron concentrate for steelmaking. By leveraging existing infrastructure and modern processing technologies, the project aims to unlock value from previously discarded material while simultaneously advancing environmental reclamation. This approach aligns economic return with environmental remediation and supports domestic iron supply.
Metallurgical test work has demonstrated the project's ability to produce a high-purity iron concentrate grading in excess of the standard 67 percent. CEO Julian Treger said that this is a validation resource’s quality and the effectiveness of the company’s processing strategy. “(It also supports) our vision of transforming a historic environmental liability into a strategic asset capable of supporting the global transition to lower-carbon steel production."
Highlights 
Inferred resource of about 71 Mt at 6.8 percent iron.
After-tax NPV7 of US$91.9 million and IRR of 29.6 percent from the recently reported Mineral Resource Estimate announced on Jun. 16, 2026
Initial capex estimated at US$65 million.
15-year mine life
A 41 percent increase in the resource according to the 2026 PEA , with a global increase in total iron grade from 6.7 to 6.8 percent.
MagIron Project
MagIron represents a restart-ready brownfield iron ore deposit, concentrator and pelletizer project in Minnesota and Indianna, that benefits from an estimated $660m in historical capital investment, targeting the production of direct-reduction grade pellets for low-carbon steelmaking. The project benefits from extensive existing infrastructure and prior capital investment, allowing rapid recommissioning compared with greenfield developments. Its strategic positioning targets rising demand for domestically sourced feedstock for electric arc furnaces and decarbonized steel production.
Senior leadership changes have been made to support the ongoing development of MagIron, especially regarding restarting its iron ore concentrator in Minnesota and pellet plant in Indiana. 
Highlights 
CoTec owns approximately 17 percent.
Definitive Feasibility Study shows after-tax NPV of about US$1.60 billion and IRR about 27.6 percent.
Average annual production is about 2.6 Mt DR-grade pellets.
Life of mine is about 32 years.
Payback period is about 3 years and 7 months.
Raised additional capital at a pre-money valuation of US$550 million from existing shareholders
CoTec Copper
CoTec Copper is a dedicated subsidiary created to accelerate the company’s exposure to copper, one of the most strategically important electrification metals. The unit focuses on acquiring and advancing copper tailings projects and sulphide deposits, particularly in historically productive mining jurisdictions where modern processing technologies can unlock additional value from previously uneconomic material. It leverages CoTec’s existing technology portfolio to enhance recoveries and lower operating costs.
Highlights 
Targets assets in Tier 1 mining regions across the United States, Australia and Africa.
Focuses on both tailings reprocessing and sulphide copper deposits.
Designed as a scalable growth platform to expand CoTec’s copper exposure.
Binding Solutions
Binding Solutions provides a cold agglomeration technology that converts ultrafine mineral waste into ISO-compliant pellets or briquettes suitable for industrial use, particularly in green steel production. Unlike traditional pelletizing processes that rely on high-temperature furnaces, this approach operates at low temperatures, drastically reducing energy consumption and emissions while enabling monetization of low-grade or waste materials.
Highlights 
Uses about 95 percent less energy than conventional pelletizing.
Generates about 98 percent fewer emissions.
Applicable to iron and other mineral fines.
Ceibo
Ceibo’s oxidative heap-leaching technology is designed to improve copper recovery from sulphide ores such as chalcopyrite, which account for the majority of global copper reserves but are traditionally difficult and costly to process. The process enhances recovery rates while lowering environmental impact and capital intensity, potentially transforming the economics of many existing copper assets.
Highlights 
Potential recovery improvement from about 31 percent via traditional leaching/concentration to approximately 70-80 percent.
Targets refractory sulphide deposits often considered uneconomic.
CoTec holds a minority equity interest and a seat on the technical advisory board.
Completed Series B C$30M financing led by Energy Impact Partners to fund the scaling of the technology.
WaveCracker
WaveCracker is a microwave-assisted mineral processing technology being advanced in collaboration with McGill University. The system uses targeted microwave energy to weaken mineral structures before conventional processing, improving metal liberation, reducing reagent consumption and lowering overall processing costs.
Highlights 
Focused initially on copper sulphide applications.
Designed to accelerate leaching and recovery kinetics.
Builds on more than 30 years of microwave mineral processing research.
Salter Cyclones
Salter Cyclones technology uses multi-gravity separators to recover ultra-fine minerals from tailings streams that traditional processing methods cannot efficiently capture. By enabling recovery of metals from waste material, the system creates new revenue streams while reducing environmental liabilities associated with tailings storage.
Highlights 
Applicable to iron, manganese and other fine mineral commodities.
Exclusive global rights for iron applications and regional exclusivity for manganese during the initial agreement period.
Converts waste into high-grade concentrates suitable for market.
Management Team
Julian Treger - Chief Executive Officer and Director
Julian Treger previously served as the CEO of Anglo Pacific Group before establishing Audley Capital Partners. At Audley, Treger directed the team through acquisitions totaling $570 million and achieved a realized Internal Rate of Return (IRR) of 38 percent. Treger continues to serve as the chairman of Audley Capital and holds both a BA and an MBA from Harvard.
Abraham Jonker - Chief Financial Officer
Abraham Jonker has 30 years of experience in mining finance. He previously served as the Lead Independent Director at Mandalay Resources and has been instrumental in leading over $750 million in equity and debt raises. Jonker is a Chartered Accountant in the UK, Canada, and South Africa and holds a Master's in Tax from Rand Afrikaans University.
John Singleton - Chief Operating Officer
John Singleton possesses over 25 years of experience in mining. His career began at De Beers, and he has since held senior leadership roles at Centamin and Rio Tinto. Singleton is a Fellow of the Royal Geological Society and holds degrees from Imperial College London and the University of Bristol.
John McGagh - Technology Consultant
John McGagh has more than 35 years of experience in digital transformation across various industries. He served as the head of innovation at Rio Tinto and is currently the chief digital officer at Snowy Hydro. McGagh is an adjunct professor at the University of Queensland and a Fellow of the Australian Academy of Technology Science and Engineering.
Eugene Hercun - VP Finance & Investor Relations
Eugene Hercun is a CPA, CA, with 15 years of varied experience in mining finance. He has led metal sales negotiations for more than $200 million annually and holds Level 1 of the CFA designation.
Board of Directors
Lucio Genovese, Independent Chairman
Lucio Genovese currently serves as the CEO of Nage Capital and as the chairman of Ferrexpo plc. He previously held senior roles at Glencore , including CEO of the CIS region. Genovese is a Chartered Accountant with degrees in Commerce and Accounting from the University of Witwatersrand.
Tom Albanese, Non - Executive Director
Tom Albanese is the former CEO of Rio Tinto and Vedanta Resources. He serves as lead independent director of Nevada Copper and as a director at Franco-Nevada Corporation. Albanese holds Master's and Bachelor's degrees from the University of Alaska Fairbanks.
Robert (Bob) Harward - Non-Executive Director
Robert Harward is a retired US Navy Vice Admiral (SEAL) and former deputy commander of US Central Command. He served on the US National Security Council and held senior strategy roles at Lockheed Martin and Shield AI.
Erez Ichilov - Non-executive Director
Erez Ichilov previously served as managing director at Traxys Projects, where he led investments in companies such as Nouveau Monde Graphite, Talon Metals, and Li-Cycle. Ichilov holds LLB and MBA degrees.
Sharon Fay - Non-executive Director
Sharon Fay previously served as head of equities and head of responsibility at AllianceBernstein. She built the firm's Corporate Responsibility and Responsible Investment teams. Fay is a Chartered Financial Analyst with a BA from Brown and an MBA from Harvard.

Tata Electronics, Besi Partner to Develop Advanced Semiconductor Packaging in India
By Nitisha Dubey

October 12, 2026 
The partnership aligns with India’s efforts to establish a domestic outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) industry 
Tata Electronics and Dutch semiconductor assembly equipment supplier Besi have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to develop advanced semiconductor packaging capabilities in India. The partnership will support Tata Electronics’ planned $3 billion semiconductor packaging facility in Jagiroad, Assam.
Under the agreement, Tata Electronics will evaluate Besi’s advanced packaging equipment and technologies for the facility. The companies will also explore local equipment support, technical collaboration and measures to ensure equipment readiness for production operations.
The collaboration will include engineering development, knowledge-sharing programmes, and specialised training and certification for Tata Electronics employees. The companies also plan to develop a joint technology roadmap and processes to address future packaging requirements and strengthen India’s semiconductor supply chain.
The partnership aligns with India’s efforts to establish a domestic outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) industry. It also follows a bilateral agreement between India and the Netherlands to strengthen cooperation in semiconductors and related emerging technologies.
- Advertisement - 
“Advanced packaging is rapidly becoming one of the most critical differentiators in semiconductor innovation,” said Dr Randhir Thakur, CEO and Managing Director of Tata Electronics. He added that combining Besi’s expertise with Tata Electronics’ expanding manufacturing capabilities would help accelerate advanced packaging development in India, foster innovation and build a semiconductor ecosystem serving domestic and global customers.
Richard Blickman, CEO and Chairman of Besi, said the company’s range of advanced packaging solutions would support Tata Electronics’ ambition to become a global semiconductor manufacturing player. He added that the collaboration reflects both companies’ commitment to innovation, technology development and the advancement of the semiconductor industry.
