Bayer to Invest $2.2 Billion in a New Manufacturing Site in Ohio
Published:
October 02, 2026
Download Press Kit
share 
New Albany, Ohio, U.S. – Ohio Governor Mike DeWine joined Bayer and JobsOhio today to announce Bayer’s plans to invest $2.2 billion in a new pharmaceutical manufacturing site in New Albany, Ohio. 
Bayer is expected to create around 600 high-value jobs in the New Albany International Business Park and roughly 1,500 construction jobs during the facility’s construction. 
“Bayer is a globally respected life sciences company that could have chosen to build this new facility anywhere in the United States — and it chose Ohio,” said Governor Mike DeWine. “This project firmly solidifies Ohio’s place among global biomanufacturing leaders as a destination for life sciences investment.” 
Building on more than $7 billion in U.S. pharma R&D and manufacturing spending over the past five years, the project is a central element of Bayer’s long-term growth strategy and commitment to innovation and patient access in its largest pharmaceuticals market. 
“Bayer has long seen the United States as a key manufacturing base and innovation hub. This landmark investment underscores our commitment,” said Bayer CEO Bill Anderson. “The new site will be home to manufacturing expertise and a skilled workforce that will strengthen our ability to deliver innovative, high-quality medicines to patients both in the United States and abroad.” 
The flexible, modular campus will be designed to combine drug substance and drug product manufacturing, leverage advanced digital and automation technologies, and support Bayer’s growing portfolio in oncology, cardiovascular and renal care. By building in Ohio, Bayer strengthens the reliability of America’s medicine supply. 
“Bayer’s $2.2 billion investment is a direct result of Ohio’s commitment to innovation and infrastructure and creating the environment for businesses to succeed,” said Senator Bernie Moreno. “We beat out many other states for this project. When completed, it could employ around 600 people making medicine here. Ohio keeps proving it is the best place in America to do business, and this does not happen without strong leadership.” 
The first module, dedicated to drug substance manufacturing, is expected to become operational in 2031. A second module for drug product manufacturing is planned to follow in 2034. The new site will complement Bayer’s U.S. pharmaceuticals headquarters in Whippany, N.J., and its other sites in Pittsburgh, Pa.; Berkeley, Calif.; Cambridge, Mass.; Research Triangle Park, N.C.; and San Diego, Calif. 
Ohio’s Biomanufacturing Workforce Readiness 
Bayer’s planned investment in a flexible, modular pharmaceutical manufacturing campus marks a major step forward for the state’s growing biomanufacturing industry and reinforces the Columbus Region’s critical mass in life sciences and biomanufacturing. 
Workforce readiness was central to Ohio's appeal. Bayer will draw on the Ohio Life Science Training Center , under construction and scheduled to open in summer 2027, to train Ohioans to work as biomanufacturing operators and technicians. JobsOhio is investing up to $30 million in the center, alongside nearly $8 million from the City of New Albany, the State of Ohio and The New Albany Company, as part of a strategy that makes life sciences an economic development priority for the state. 
“Bayer didn't just choose a site. It chose a workforce,” said JobsOhio President and CEO J.P. Nauseef. “The Ohio Life Science Training Center exists to prepare Ohioans for careers in STEM, and it's already paying off. Together, JobsOhio, Ohio Life Sciences, the City of New Albany and Columbus State are building the talent pipeline that will ensure the future of medicine is built in Ohio.” 
Infrastructure that Supports the Speed of Business 
Best-in-class infrastructure and shovel-ready sites are among the reasons CNBC named Ohio the No. 1 state for business in 2026. Two decades of master planning in New Albany to ensure access to power, water, and infrastructure allow projects like this move quickly. Bayer joins a growing life sciences cluster in the New Albany International Business Park that includes Amgen, Hims & Hers, American Regent and Pharmavite. 
These companies benefit from operating inside the Ohio Discovery Corridor — which connects nine world-class medical and research facilities and leading academic institutions — providing access to 39,000 annual STEM graduates, a $1B annual NIH-funded research engine and collaborative partnerships that drive ground-breaking research and innovation. 
“Bayer’s investment builds upon the momentum we are creating both locally and statewide, including the recently announced Ohio Life Science Training Center. The New Albany International Business Park will be home to the nearly $38 million, state-of-the-art biomanufacturing training facility, the first of its kind in Ohio,” said New Albany Mayor Sloan Spalding. “Together, these investments are creating high-value career opportunities and building the workforce needed to support the continued growth of this important industry.” 
The new Bayer facility will also form part of a new U.S.-based collaboration ecosystem. The ambition is to connect cutting-edge academic innovation with advanced manufacturing expertise to create a strong ecosystem that supports future-ready pharmaceutical production.   
“Bayer’s decision is a powerful statement about the Columbus Region’s growing position as a global center for life sciences,” said Jonas Peterson, chief economic development officer and president of One Columbus. “Our location provides exceptional access to major North American markets, while our talent has the depth to support the sophisticated work driving the future of medicine. Bayer is joining a region with real momentum in life sciences, and the capacity and ambition to lead what comes next.” 
The Bayer project will pursue a Job Creation Tax Credit from the Ohio Department of Development at a future Tax Credit Authority meeting. The company also plans to pursue JobsOhio assistance for the project, which would be made public after a final agreement is executed. 
What They’re Saying 
This is a big investment for my district and for Central Ohio. Bayer’s $2 billion investment means 600 new jobs and more opportunities for our families. Announcements like this show why companies around the world are choosing our region to invest, innovate, and create jobs. I’m especially excited to be part of building a workforce pipeline that prepares Ohioans to compete for these jobs and build careers in the life sciences industry. I look forward to working with Bayer and the new training center to make sure our workforce is ready to take advantage of these opportunities. This is what it looks like when we work together to deliver for Central Ohio. 
-Congresswoman Joyce Beatty (OH-03) 
Today’s announcement is the latest example of how President Trump’s economic policies are making America — and Ohio — stronger, more prosperous, and more secure. Congratulations to Bayer and the people of Ohio on this major investment in the state’s economy and workforce. 
- Jeffrey Kessler , Under Secretary of Commerce for Industry and Security. 
The United States is a key market for Bayer’s Pharmaceuticals division. This expansion is another important step to grow our pharmaceuticals business and to meet the demand of our customers and patients in the U.S., our fastest-growing pharmaceuticals market, and beyond. 
- Sebastian Guth , Chief Operating Officer, Bayer Pharmaceuticals and President, Bayer U.S. 
The facility will be a strong strategic addition to our global Product Supply network. As we continue to invest in our existing manufacturing sites around the globe, our planned presence in Ohio will further enhance our ability to serve our markets with greater resilience and reliability. 
- Holger Weintritt , Head of Product Supply at Bayer’s Pharmaceuticals division 
Bayer’s decision to expand its presence in Ohio is great news for innovation and economic growth in our state. This new facility will open new opportunities for consequential academic-industry partnerships and scientific discoveries that will transform the future of healthcare and the life sciences. We’re excited for Ohio State researchers to work alongside Bayer teams toward our shared goals, and we’re especially proud of the integral role that our university and Ohio higher education partners play in securing economic wins like this for our state.  
- Ravi Bellamkonda , president of The Ohio State University 
Our region is primed to drive the next wave of biopharmaceutical growth. The New Albany Business Park supports this momentum, having attracted global life sciences companies American Regent, Amgen and Pharmavite, among others, to establish and grow their Ohio footprint. These industry leaders already employ more than 2,660 people in our Business Park, a total bolstered by Amgen’s 350 job expansion opening in New Albany in 2027. To sustain this growth, the Ohio Life Science Training Center will launch in New Albany in 2027, equipping potential employees with the skills needed for advanced manufacturing opportunities. We celebrate the commitment of Bayer, a leading global biopharmaceutical company that will provide more high-paying jobs and investment that benefits our state and the greater Columbus region.
-William Ebbing , President and CEO, The New Albany Company 
Ohio wins transformational investments like this because we listen to industry and act early. Bayer told us workforce readiness was essential, and our collective investment in the Ohio Life Science Training Center gave them confidence that Ohio can deliver.
- Eddie Pauline , President and CEO, Ohio Life Sciences 
The opportunity to connect education with a growing industry, expose students to future career pathways and help them understand the skills needed for high-quality, good-paying jobs is incredibly valuable. We look forward to exploring opportunities to build meaningful connections that benefit our students, our schools and the greater New Albany community. 
- Dr. Jason Fine , Superintendent, New Albany-Plain Local Schools 
About Bayer 
Bayer is a global enterprise with core competencies in the life science fields of health care and nutrition. In line with its mission, “Health for all, Hunger for none,” the company’s products and services are designed to support efforts to master major challenges presented by a growing and aging global population and create value through innovation and growth. The Bayer brand stands for trust, reliability and quality throughout the world. In fiscal 2025, the Group employed around 88,000 people and had sales of 45.6 billion euros. R&D expenses amounted to 5.8 billion euros. For more information, go to www.bayer.com . 
About JobsOhio 
JobsOhio, Ohio's private nonprofit economic development corporation, enhances company growth and personnel development through business attraction, retention, and expansion across ten competitive industry sectors. With a team of seasoned professionals, JobsOhio utilizes a comprehensive network to foster talent production in targeted industries and attract talent through  Find Your Ohio . Collaborating with seven regional partners, including  Dayton Development Coalition ,  Lake to River Economic Development ,  Ohio Southeast Economic Development ,  One Columbus ,  REDI Cincinnati ,  Regional Growth Partnership , and  Team NEO , JobsOhio delivers world-class customer service to provide companies with a competitive advantage. Learn more at www.jobsohio.com. Follow us on  LinkedIn ,  X , and  Facebook . 
About the Ohio Discovery Corridor 
The Ohio Discovery Corridor connects nine anchor institutions — Case Western Reserve University, Cincinnati Cancer Center, Cincinnati Children’s, Cleveland Clinic, Cleveland State University, Nationwide Children’s Hospital, The Ohio State University, University Hospitals, and the University of Cincinnati — across Cleveland, Columbus, and Cincinnati to form the state’s life science innovation platform. This network provides companies with access to 39,000 annual STEM graduates, a $1B annual NIH-funded research engine, and physical space needed to bring innovative medicines and devices from benchtop to bedside. Powered by a $400+ million investment from JobsOhio and the State of Ohio, the Ohio Discovery Corridor is building the workforce, technology, and infrastructure to prepare the state and the world for the future of the life sciences industry. If you or your company are interested in joining us as we build, visit OhioDiscoveryCorridor.com .

content_text:
Rauschenberger leaves Siemens Energy’s investment arm 
Oct 1, 2026 • Oishani Mitra 
Kendra Rauschenberger has taken on the role of vice president of global sales for onshore wind at Siemens Gamesa. 
Kendra Rauschenberger has left her position as general partner at Siemens Energy Ventures, the corporate VC arm of German energy technology company Siemens Energy, after six and a half years to take on the role of vice president of global sales for onshore wind at Siemens Gamesa.
A GCV Powerlister , Rauschenberger was one of the founding members of Siemens Energy Ventures and played a role growing the unit into “a platform across venture building, venture clienting and venture capital capabilities that is delivering impact and is now embedded in how Siemens Energy approaches innovation and solves business challenges”.
The move to Siemens Gamesa marks a return to wind power for Rauschenberger, who started her journey there when she joined Siemens Energy in 2000 as a trainee.
“I am excited to join the Onshore Wind team at a time when our industry is evolving rapidly and the demand for clean, reliable and affordable energy has never been greater. I look forward to learning and building the future together with colleagues, customers and partners around the world as we help shape the future of energy,” she said in the LinkedIn post announcing her move.
Siemens Energy Ventures was launched in 2020 and works with cleantech startups through venture capital, partnerships, venture building and venture clienting.

title: Applied Materials and Besi Expand AI Advanced Packaging Partnership Through EPIC Center - Yahoo Finance
query: "Applied Materials" ("press release" OR "investor relations" OR earnings OR announcement OR investment OR expansion OR acquisition OR partnership OR Korea) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
Applied Materials and Besi Expand AI Advanced Packaging Partnership Through EPIC Center
Fiona Craig 
October 1, 2026 3 min read 
AMAT 
+9.72% 
Artificial intelligence applications ©Shutterstock The expanded collaboration moves beyond hybrid bonding into 3D IC integration, thermo-compression bonding, panel-scale packaging and photonics technologies designed to support AI system scaling. 
Key Investor Takeaways 
Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT) and Besi (EU:BESI) are expanding their AI advanced packaging partnership, with Besi becoming an Innovation Partner at Applied's EPIC Center. 
The companies will broaden joint development beyond hybrid bonding into 3D IC scaling, thermo-compression bonding, die-on-panel integration and photonics-enabled interconnects. 
The partnership targets higher-density and higher-bandwidth connections required for increasingly complex AI compute and memory architectures. 
Besi engineers will work alongside Applied teams at the EPIC Center, potentially giving mutual customers earlier access to jointly developed packaging processes. 
Applied expects capital spending on its new Silicon Valley EPIC Center to scale over time to approximately $5 billion as customer projects begin. 
Why AMAT Stock Is in Focus 
Applied Materials is expanding its semiconductor packaging collaboration with Besi as AI infrastructure increases requirements for higher-density chip interconnects. 
Besi will join Applied's EPIC Center as an Innovation Partner, extending a relationship that began with a joint development programme in 2020. The companies previously established a Center of Excellence in Singapore that combined Applied's semiconductor process technologies with Besi's die placement and assembly capabilities. 
That work produced Kinex, which the companies describe as the industry's first integrated die-to-wafer hybrid bonding system. 
The expanded programme will cover a wider portion of the advanced packaging process. Planned R&D includes new die-to-wafer hybrid bonding platforms, scaling of thermo-compression bonding, die-on-wafer, die-on-die and die-on-panel integration, and photonics-enabled interconnects for co-packaged optics and AI systems. 
The work is expected to focus particularly on next-generation 3D IC scaling and integration between logic and memory. 
Why This Matters for Investors 
The partnership positions advanced packaging as a larger part of Applied Materials' AI-related technology roadmap. As AI systems require increasingly close integration between compute, memory and other components, the manufacturing challenge extends beyond producing individual chips to connecting them efficiently within larger systems. 
Expanding the Besi partnership may allow Applied to address more of that integration process by combining its materials engineering and wafer-processing expertise with Besi's assembly and bonding technologies. 
Story Continues 
The collaboration could also shorten development cycles by bringing the two companies' engineers together with logic, memory and systems companies at the EPIC Center. According to Applied, the facility is intended to reduce the time required to move semiconductor technologies from early research into high-volume manufacturing. 
For investors, the announcement does not provide new revenue targets or financial guidance. Its significance instead lies in the companies broadening an existing technology partnership as advanced packaging becomes increasingly important to AI compute scaling. 
What to Watch Next 
Key developments will include the start of R&D programmes at the EPIC Center and progress toward new hybrid bonding, TCB, panel-level and photonics integration platforms. 
Investors can also watch for evidence that jointly developed technologies move from research into customer qualification and high-volume manufacturing, particularly as Applied's EPIC Center becomes operationally ready this year.

Heraeus Medical Components broke ground May 2 for a 17,000-square-foot addition to its facility in White Bear Township.
The company, one of the world's leading medical component manufacturers, currently employs 340 workers at 5030 Centerville Road, making it one of White Bear Township's largest employers. An additional 55 jobs will be created and a sum close to the two-digit-million-dollar-range will be invested in the expansion, qualifying Heraeus for nearly $500,000 under the Minnesota DEED Awards First Job Creation Funds Project.
Heraeus Medical Components General Manager Keith Foerster said: "We are excited to be launching our second expansion effort in the last four years. The proximity to our customers, availability of a talented workforce and our ongoing relationship with White Bear Township were key factors in our decision to expand in Minnesota."
Headquartered in Germany, Heraeus' precious metals and technology group is a global, private company founded 160 years ago. In the financial year 2012, Heraeus generated product revenues of almost $4 billion and previous metal trading revenues of $16 billion.
